The zone is taken from the GRI value: A up to 20, B up to 40, C up to 60, D up to 80, E above 80. GRI is shown for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active, as GMI. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. Always calculated with the consensus ranges.None

Hypoglycemia event (CGM Report)Level 1: counted after at least 15 consecutive minutes below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), starting at the first of those readings. Level 2 (counted separately): counted after at least 15 consecutive minutes below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L), starting at the first of those readings. Every event, level 2 included, ends after at least 15 consecutive minutes at or above 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L). Level 2 events are also counted as level 1 events. The 2017 international consensus states that "readings below the threshold for at least 15 min" are considered an event and that the event ends with readings for 15 minutes at 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or higher {cite:danne2017|Section 4, para. 14}. This explains how the level 1 and level 2 events in the Hypoglycemia section are counted: an event is counted once its readings have been below its limit for 15 minutes, starts at its first reading below the limit, and ends with 15 minutes at 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or higher. For clinical trials, the 2023 consensus ends a level 2 event after 15 minutes at or above 54 mg/dL {cite:battelino2023|Table 4}. A data gap ({gap_rule}, the reading interval being the median of the 10 intervals before the reading; see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}) also ends an event, and a run below the limit starts again after it. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.None

Sensor active (data received by GlucoCraft)Percentage of the period represented by the readings received (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}). {sensor_active_note}Condition for the targets, not a target: at least 70% over 14 days {cite:battelino2019|Table 2} (the ADA Standards list the same, {cite:ada2026|Table 6.2})
Minimum, maximum, readingsObserved values.None
"None" indicates that no consensus target has been published for the metric. The value and its definition are shown without assessment.
What the cited sources say about these metrics

Time below range. The ADA Standards of Care state that 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) "has been recognized as a threshold for adrenergic responses to falling glucose in people without diabetes" and that level 2, below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L), "is the threshold at which neuroglycopenic symptoms begin to occur" {cite:ada2026|Hypoglycemia Definitions and Event Rates section, para. 1}. This explains the two limits of the Time Below 70 and Time Below 54 rows.

Time above range. The 2019 international consensus sets the targets for time above range at less than 25% above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and less than 5% above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L), which are less than 6 hours and less than 1 hour and 12 minutes per day {cite:battelino2019|Table 3}. The 25% target covers levels 1 and 2 together and so includes the time above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) {cite:ada2026|Table 6.2}. The 2019 consensus defines level 1 hyperglycemia as 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L) and level 2 as above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) {cite:battelino2019|Table 2}. This explains the targets in the rows of the time above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) and above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L).

Time in tight range. The 2017 international consensus on the use of CGM lists 70–140 mg/dL (3.9–7.8 mmol/L) as a secondary target range {cite:danne2017}. The 2023 international consensus statement for clinical trials calls the time in this range time in tight range and, for clinical trials that use it, suggests a target of more than 70% {cite:battelino2023}. The 2019 consensus for clinical care and the ADA Standards of Care set no target for it {cite:ada2026,battelino2019}. For this reason, the Time in Tight Range row has no target and is shown without green or red.

Data sufficiency. The ADA Standards of Care list two conditions for valid CGM data: at least 14 days of wear, and the CGM active for 70% of the time over those 14 days {cite:ada2026|Table 6.2}. The 2019 international consensus gives the same 14 days and 70%, counted as a share of the possible CGM readings {cite:battelino2019|Table 2}. For this reason, ✓ / ✗ and green / red are shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active, and the values of a period of any length only with at least 70% (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Enough data); GlucoCraft measures sensor active as the share of the period represented by the readings received (GlucoCraft rule).

Coefficient of variation. The 2019 international consensus sets the target for glycemic variability at a coefficient of variation (%CV) of 36% or less {cite:battelino2019|Table 2}, a value it takes from {ref:monnier2017|Monnier et al.} (2017). The ADA Standards of Care list the same goal of 36% or less {cite:ada2026|Table 6.2}. This explains the target in the CV row. The 2017 international consensus states that "CV should be considered the primary measure of variability" and describes the standard deviation as "a key secondary glycemic variability measure" {cite:danne2017|Section 5, para. 11}. This explains why the CV row carries the variability target; the 2019 consensus and the ADA Standards of Care publish no target for the standard deviation ({ref:ada2026}, Table 6.2; {ref:battelino2019}, Table 2). The 2017 international consensus defines stable glucose levels as a CV below 36% and unstable glucose levels as a CV of 36% or higher {cite:danne2017|Section 5}. The 2019 consensus target is a CV of 36% or less {cite:battelino2019|Table 2}, so a CV of exactly 36% meets the 2019 target and is in the 2017 unstable range. This explains where the 36% value in the CV row comes from; GlucoCraft compares the CV with the 2019 target (GlucoCraft rule, following the treatment standards).

GMI. The ADA Standards of Care describe GMI as a "calculated value approximating A1C (not always equivalent)" and state, for mean glucose and GMI, that "goals for these values are not standardized" {cite:ada2026|Table 6.2}. This explains why the GMI row is marked "not a laboratory A1C" and has no target. {ref:bergenstal2018|Bergenstal et al.} (2018), who introduced GMI, suggest that "at least 10 and preferably 14 or more days of CGM data" be used to calculate it {cite:bergenstal2018|How Is GMI Calculated? section, para. 5}. This explains why GMI is shown only for periods of 14 days or more with at least 70% sensor active. {ref:bergenstal2018|Bergenstal et al.} (2018) calculate GMI from the mean CGM glucose as GMI (%) = 3.31 + 0.02392 × mean glucose in mg/dL, a formula derived from 528 people in four randomized trials {cite:bergenstal2018|How Is GMI Calculated? section, Figure 1}. This explains how the GMI value is calculated.

GMI in mmol/mol. The GMI study gives two equations: GMI (%) = 3.31 + 0.02392 × mean glucose in mg/dL, and GMI (mmol/mol) = 12.71 + 4.70587 × mean glucose in mmol/L {cite:bergenstal2018}. GlucoCraft calculates the mean in mg/dL and converts it to mmol/L for the second equation with the factor 18.016, the factor it uses for every conversion. The study's two equations fit each other most closely with a factor of about 18.0. The difference changes the GMI in mmol/mol by 1 for about 1 in 20 mean values and never changes the GMI in percent. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.

Glycemia Risk Index. {ref:klonoff2023|Klonoff et al.} (2023) define a hypoglycemia component, the percentage of time below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) plus 0.8 × the percentage at 54–69 mg/dL (3.0–3.8 mmol/L), and a hyperglycemia component, the percentage above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) plus 0.5 × the percentage at 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L); the GRI is 3.0 × the hypoglycemia component + 1.6 × the hyperglycemia component, capped at 100 {cite:klonoff2023|Development of the GRI section}. They state that the two components "should be calculated and displayed separately" {cite:klonoff2023|Abstract, para. 3}. This explains the GRI value and the separate hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia values beside it. {ref:klonoff2023|Klonoff et al.} (2023) describe the GRI as "not a substitute for looking at individual metrics" but as a summary score {cite:klonoff2023|Limitations section, para. 2}. This explains why the GRI is shown together with the time-in-range values from which it is calculated, not in place of them.

Other groups. The consensus also publishes different targets for some groups, such as older or high-risk adults and pregnancy ({ref:battelino2019}, Tables 3 and 4: the published article). They are not included here. The results here are calculated with the ranges and targets for adults in general, not with the ranges for these groups.
docs.section.studies.title: Published Findings
docs.section.studies.body: The following findings from published research concern study populations. They are reported as stated by the authors and are not statements about an individual; GlucoCraft does not apply them to individual results. Where a study measured A1C (a laboratory test) rather than CGM data, this is stated.
Time in range
<ul>
• The 2019 international consensus associates each 5-percentage-point increase in time in range with clinically significant benefits for people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes {cite:battelino2019}.

• The 2023 consensus statement for clinical trials states that the international consensus has accepted a change of at least 5 percentage points in time in range as clinically meaningful for an individual trial participant, and 3 percentage points between the groups of a trial {cite:battelino2023}.

• In the DCCT, among 1,440 people with type 1 diabetes whose time in range was estimated from quarterly 7-point fingerstick profiles (not CGM), each 10-percentage-point lower time in range was associated with a 64% higher hazard of retinopathy progression and a 40% higher hazard of microalbuminuria {cite:beck2019}.

• In a cross-sectional study of 3,262 adults with type 2 diabetes using CGM, lower time in range was associated with diabetic retinopathy at all severity grades after adjustment for A1C {cite:lu2018}.

• Among 6,225 adults with type 2 diabetes followed for a median of 6.9 years, a baseline time in range of 50% or less was associated with hazard ratios of 1.83 for all-cause mortality and 1.85 for cardiovascular mortality, compared with a time in range above 85% {cite:lu2021}.

• Among 163 adults with type 1 diabetes, each 5-percentage-point lower time in range over up to 7 years of CGM data was associated with 18% higher odds of incident diabetic retinopathy {cite:shah2024}.

• In the analysis summarized by the 2019 international consensus, among 545 adults with type 1 diabetes, a time in range of 70% and 50% corresponded to an A1C of about 7% (53 mmol/mol) and 8% (64 mmol/mol), and each 10 percentage points more time in range (2 hours and 24 minutes per day) to an A1C about 0.5 percentage points (5.5 mmol/mol) lower {cite:battelino2019|Relationship Between TIR and A1C section, Table 5}. This describes study populations; it is not a prediction for an individual.
Hypoglycemia
<ul>

• The International Hypoglycaemia Study Group classifies glucose below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) as clinically significant hypoglycemia {cite:ihsg2017}; subsequent consensus reports designate it level 2 {cite:danne2017,battelino2019}.
Glycemic variability
<ul>
• The 36% threshold was proposed by {ref:monnier2017|Monnier et al.} (2017), in a study of 376 people with diabetes who used CGM.

• In a meta-analysis of cohort studies, greater visit-to-visit variability of A1C (not CGM) was associated with renal, retinal and cardiovascular events and, in type 2 diabetes, with higher mortality, independent of A1C level {cite:gorst2015}.

• In a 2025 meta-analysis of observational studies including approximately 4.2 million adults, high long-term variability of A1C or fasting glucose (not CGM) was associated with a hazard ratio of 1.69 for incident heart failure {cite:li2025}.

• Among 28,016 people with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes followed for 10 years, A1C trajectories that remained low and stable were associated with fewer microvascular events than unstable trajectories, after adjustment for mean A1C; one unstable trajectory was associated with higher mortality, and none with more macrovascular events {cite:laiteerapong2017}.
A1C and GMI
<ul>

• The GMI formula, its derivation and the days of data it needs are described in {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}; the agreement of GMI with laboratory A1C in {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF. A mean glucose of 154 mg/dL (8.5 mmol/L) corresponds to a calculated GMI of approximately 7.0% (53 mmol/mol; calculated by GlucoCraft).

• The Standards of Care of the American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee consider an A1C below 7% appropriate for many nonpregnant adults without severe hypoglycemia or frequent hypoglycemia affecting health or quality of life {cite:ada2025|Recommendation 6.3a} and, for CGM users, set goals of more than 70% time in range, less than 4% below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and less than 1% below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L); GMI is listed without a standardized goal {cite:ada2025}. The 2026 edition retains the A1C goal {cite:ada2026}.

• In the UKPDS observational analysis of people with type 2 diabetes, each 1-percentage-point reduction in updated mean A1C was associated with 21% fewer diabetes-related deaths, 14% fewer myocardial infarctions and 37% fewer microvascular complications {cite:stratton2000}.

• In the DCCT/EDIC study of people with type 1 diabetes, the study group with the lower A1C during the trial had lower complication rates for decades after the A1C levels of the groups converged, an effect the investigators term "metabolic memory" {cite:nathan2014|EDIC/Metabolic Memory section, para. 1}.

• Among 34,737 people with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, an A1C of 6.5% or higher during the first year after diagnosis was associated with more microvascular events, and an A1C of 7.0% or higher with higher mortality, over a mean follow-up of 13 years (the "legacy effect") {cite:laiteerapong2019|Abstract, para. 1}.
Length of the data period
<ul>

• Among 257 people with type 1 diabetes, 14 days of CGM data estimated 3-month mean glucose, time in range and time above range closely (R² 0.84–0.86); the agreement was lower for time below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L; 0.76) and CV (0.70) {cite:riddlesworth2018}.

• Among 329 people with type 1 diabetes with 90 days of CGM data, the error of time below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L) compared with the full 90 days was 47% with 10 days, 26% with 30 days and 11% with 60 days of data, against 10%, 5% and 2% for time in range {cite:cichosz2023}.
• The 2019 consensus states that more variable glycemia may require 4 weeks of data to assess hypoglycemia {cite:battelino2019}.
Glycemia Risk Index and reports
<ul>

• The Glycemia Risk Index was derived from rankings by 330 clinicians of 225 14-day CGM tracings of adults and correlated closely with those rankings (r = 0.95); zones A–E correspond to the quintiles of the ranking {cite:klonoff2023}.

• The Ambulatory Glucose Profile, first described by Mazze et al. (1987, as cited in {ref:bergenstal2013}), was recommended as a standardized CGM report by an expert panel in 2013 {cite:bergenstal2013}. Its current form shows the percentiles 5, 25, 50, 75 and 95 by time of day {cite:battelino2023|p. 49}.
docs.section.left_out.title: What GlucoCraft Leaves Out, and Why
docs.section.left_out.body: GlucoCraft shows cited information about the results it calculates (see {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources} and {sec:studies|Published Findings}). Some research and recommendations are left out on purpose. The categories below state what is left out and why; the sources are listed by citation only, and their content is not restated here.

• Treatment recommendations. Recommendations on insulin, other medication, dosing, food or physical activity are left out, because GlucoCraft calculates and displays results and gives no advice about treatment. Such recommendations are part of the Standards of Care, Sections 6 and 7 {cite:ada2026,ada2026b}, and of the consensus statements {cite:battelino2019,danne2017}, for example a footnote on CV targets {cite:battelino2019|Table 2}.

• Targets for specific groups. The targets that the consensus publishes for older or high-risk adults and for pregnancy are left out, because GlucoCraft's results are calculated with the ranges and targets for adults in general only {cite:battelino2019|Tables 3 and 4}. The publication is linked in {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources} (Other groups).

• Device and laboratory accuracy. Statements about the accuracy of CGM systems, blood glucose meters and laboratory tests, and about factors that affect sensor readings or laboratory A1C, are left out, because they are a matter for the CGM manufacturers and laboratories and are stated in their own documentation ({ref:abbott}, p. 18; {ref:ada2026}, {ref_year:ada2026b}, Table 7.4).

• Findings that cannot be stated without naming medications or substances. Findings whose study groups or results are defined by a medication or a substance are left out, because the cited context beside GlucoCraft's results names no medication or substance: for example a finding on variability {cite:monnier2017}, a post-trial follow-up of long-term outcomes {cite:holman2008}, a definition of remission {cite:riddle2021}, a statement on the risk of hypoglycemia {cite:ada2026|Hypoglycemia Risk Assessment section} and the treatment of the people studied for the GRI ({ref:klonoff2023}, Abstract).
These works were consulted while GlucoCraft was designed and are not used in its texts, each for the reason given.
• Section 7 of the 2025 Standards of Care {cite:ada2025b}: the 2026 edition of the same section is cited instead {cite:ada2026b}.
• Sections 13, 14 and 15 of the 2026 Standards of Care {cite:ada2026c,ada2026d,ada2026e}: their goals and recommendations are for specific groups (see Targets for specific groups above).
• Two clinical practice consensus guidelines {cite:sundberg2022,tauschmann2024}: their targets and recommendations are for specific groups.
• A review on time in tight range {cite:sundberg2025}: consulted for the definition of time in tight range, which GlucoCraft cites from its source {cite:battelino2023}.

• Two handouts on the review of CGM data {cite:idc2024a,idc2024b}: they describe a review method of clinical care, which belongs to treatment, and a comparison of weekdays and weekends that GlucoCraft does not calculate.

• A sample report with time in tight range {cite:idc2025}: it prints goals that neither the consensus statements nor the Standards of Care publish; GlucoCraft shows the time in tight range without a target (see {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}).
• An article on the standardized report in clinical practice {cite:johnson2019}: only its abstract could be read.

• A study of the relationship between A1C and time in range {cite:vigersky2019}: the study itself was not read; its estimate is known only as the 2019 consensus reports it {cite:battelino2019|Table 5}.
Other research items, for example on measures that GlucoCraft does not calculate, are kept for possible later use and are not shown.
docs.section.notifications.title: Notifications (Not Alarms)
docs.section.notifications.body: Notifications are not alarms. GlucoCraft's notifications depend on the data source, the network and Home Assistant, and may be delayed or not delivered.
No high or low glucose notifications. GlucoCraft sends no notifications about high or low glucose.

• Delivery. Notifications are created as Home Assistant notifications (the bell in the sidebar; the no-data notice only while No-data notice is on), which produce no sound. Each kind of GlucoCraft notification has one place in Home Assistant's notifications (the wall-panel notices one per panel): a new daily summary, for example, replaces the previous one.

• Phones (optional). Phones and other notify actions selected in GlucoCraft's settings ({screen_notifications} > Also send notifications to) receive the notification types selected under Notifications to send there in addition (the summaries and the no-data notice, each only when selected). A message to a phone has the same text as the Home Assistant notification. It is an ordinary notification, with no priority, sound or channel of its own: the phone shows it according to its own notification settings. Notifications can be sent to more than one phone. A phone is listed once the Home Assistant Companion app is installed and signed in. Send a test notification now sends one test message, GlucoCraft delivery test; its arrival does not show that later messages will arrive. The requirements for delivery are listed on Settings Status; even when they are met, messages may be delayed or not delivered. A delivery that fails is recorded as a warning in the Home Assistant log (Settings > System > Logs); no other message is shown.
• Privacy. Messages to a phone contain the glucose value. How a notification reaches a phone is decided by Home Assistant's Companion app (see its documentation).

• Summaries (the daily summary is on by default, the weekly summary off; {screen_notifications}: Daily summary, Daily summary time, Weekly summary, Weekly summary day). The daily summary, at the configured time (default 08:00): the last reading, the sensor expiry (where a sensor expiry entity is set) and the rolling 24 hours, with the time in range of the last 14 days compared with the last 90 days. The weekly summary (rolling 7 and 14 days, and the time in range of the last 14 days compared with the last 90 days), on the configured day at the same time (default Sunday). The monthly summary (rolling 30 and 90 days and 6 months, and the time in range of the last 30 days compared with the last 90 days and with the last 6 months), sent with the weekly summary in calendar weeks 4, 8, 12 and so on (ISO week numbers); turning the weekly summary off also stops the monthly summary. A summary whose time passes while Home Assistant is not running is not sent later. They are titled GlucoCraft Daily Summary, GlucoCraft Weekly Summary and GlucoCraft Monthly Summary. Each summary lists the values of its periods beside the consensus targets and, while the ranges in use differ from the consensus ranges, each period's time in, below and above the custom ranges; a comparison of time in range is listed only when both periods compared have enough data, and in the weekly and monthly summaries only when the difference of the two values as shown is 5 percentage points or more. Each period of a summary (24 hours, 7, 14, 30 or 90 days, or 6 months) shows its values only when the sensor has covered at least 70% of it (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Enough data), the same for a source that reads every minute and one that reads every 15 minutes; otherwise the summary states for that period that there is not enough data yet, how much the sensor has covered and about how much longer it takes with no gaps. A summary is created also then. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. The actions glucocraft.send_daily_summary, glucocraft.send_weekly_summary and glucocraft.send_monthly_summary send a summary immediately, also while the scheduled summary is off.

• No-data notice (optional, off by default; {screen_notifications}: No-data notice, Notify after). A notice, titled GlucoCraft No-Data Notice, that GlucoCraft has received no readings since a given time, never about glucose; see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}.

• Wall-panel notices (Home Assistant notifications only, not sent to phones): GlucoCraft Panel Added when a wall panel is connected for the first time, naming its shape and the display card in use; GlucoCraft Panel Offline when a panel's Status entity has been off or unavailable for 10 minutes, removed when the panel is connected again.

• Other notices. GlucoCraft CGM Report after each print that was started (printed or not, the reason, and the name of the PDF kept, when one was made; a period or an appendix that is not available is refused by the action, without a notice); GlucoCraft export after a CSV export; GlucoCraft Wall-Panel Address when a new wall-panel address is created (it names the settings screen where administrators find the address and does not contain it); GlucoCraft import after a CSV import; GlucoCraft deleted after a removal that kept the readings for a reinstall.

• Repair notices (Settings > System > Repairs): Glucose source without a unit, when a source without a unit of measurement reports values that indicate mmol/L (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}); Glucose source is too slow for live display, when a source's readings arrive every 15 minutes or less often (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}); Glucose source may have stopped: the same value for over an hour, from a source without its own measurement time (see {sec:cgms|Supported Sources}); Glucose source stays at …, the sensor cap notices, when a source's readings repeatedly stop at exactly {value_400} or {value_450} {unit}, or at {value_50} {unit}; Glucose source stays at its upper limit, …, as a number and Glucose source stays at its lower limit, …, as a number; Glucose source sends numbers below the sensor lower limit set by hand and Glucose source sends numbers above the sensor upper limit set by hand; The very-low limit is below the glucose sensor's lower limit and The very-high limit is above the glucose sensor's upper limit (for these, see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}); CGM sensor expiry entity not found, CGM sensor expiry entity holds no expiry and CGM sensor expiry entity shows an expiry long past (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Sensor expiry); A GlucoCraft entity is set as a glucose source; Stored glucose readings are later than the system clock; The system clock may be ahead of the glucose readings; Glucose source with a unit other than mg/dL or mmol/L; Glucose source not found; GlucoCraft could not read the glucose history; GlucoCraft's cards could not be added to the dashboards; GlucoCraft's dashboard could not be added, when Home Assistant did not accept GlucoCraft's dashboard (GlucoCraft tries again at its next start); Glucose source states mmol/L with values that look like another unit, after 10 readings in a row above 33.3 mmol/L (they are still used, as HI); Glucose source states mg/dL with values that look like mmol/L, after 10 readings in a row below 30 mg/dL (they are still treated as mg/dL: no reading, or LO); Measurement-time attribute holds no usable time, after 10 readings in a row without one under the name set in the settings; Glucose source updates too often to add readings, after at least 10 minutes of new values less than 15 seconds apart; GlucoCraft put its entity ids back, when an entity was given another id while GlucoCraft was running (a new name for a device can change its entity ids): the cards, the dashboard and the wall panels find their entities by those ids, so GlucoCraft gives the original id back within seconds and says so, in a notice that stays until it is dismissed; Entity ids of GlucoCraft were changed, for a change it could not undo, made while GlucoCraft was not running or when another entity has the original id: the notice lists them and puts them back; and five notices about the readings file: GlucoCraft's readings file was damaged; the readings were recovered, GlucoCraft's readings file was damaged, GlucoCraft's readings file could not be read, GlucoCraft's readings file could not be written and GlucoCraft's readings file is from a newer version of GlucoCraft (for these, see {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}). While any of these notices is open and not ignored, the display card and the wall panels show Check Home Assistant in the status bar (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).
docs.section.automations.title: Automations
docs.section.automations.body: GlucoCraft's entities are ordinary Home Assistant entities, listed in {sec:entities|Entity Names}. Like any Home Assistant entity, they are available to other dashboards, automations and scripts. GlucoCraft provides no automation examples.
docs.section.install.title: Installing, Updating and Removing GlucoCraft
docs.section.install.body: GlucoCraft is not in the default catalog of Home Assistant's Marketplace or of HACS: it is installed from its repository, https://github.com/Verstreubulator/glucocraft, as a custom repository, or by hand. Each way ends with the setup (Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > GlucoCraft; see {sec:setup|Setup}), after a restart of Home Assistant for an installation through HACS or by hand; an installation through the Marketplace needs no restart.

• Home Assistant 2026.11 and later: the Marketplace. In Settings > Marketplace, the repository's address is added as a custom repository with the category Integration, and GlucoCraft is installed. The Marketplace asks for a connection to GitHub for a custom repository and checks the repository before it installs it. An installation made with HACS before the update to 2026.11 is taken over by the Marketplace, with its custom repositories.
• Home Assistant 2026.3.1 to 2026.10: HACS. In HACS, the menu (three dots) > Custom repositories, the repository's address with the type Integration, Add; then GlucoCraft > Download.
• By hand. The folder custom_components/glucocraft/ of the repository is copied into the folder custom_components/ of the Home Assistant configuration.

• A new version. A version installed through the Marketplace or HACS is updated from its update entity under Settings > Updates; a version installed by hand by copying the new folder over the old one. A restart of Home Assistant completes the update. The settings, the stored readings and the wall-panel address are kept.
• Learning of a new version. Each new version is published as a release of the repository: the update entity shows it, and watching the repository's releases on GitHub announces it.

• After an update. A dashboard page that was open is reloaded once (see {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}). A wall panel keeps its firmware until it is built again from the updated example configuration.

• Removing GlucoCraft (Settings > Devices & services > GlucoCraft > the menu (three dots) > Delete; then a restart of Home Assistant, and the removal of GlucoCraft in the Marketplace or in HACS, together with its custom repository, or of the folder custom_components/glucocraft/ of an installation by hand). Deleting GlucoCraft removes its settings, its dashboard and its wall-panel address: a new installation starts with the default settings, and every wall panel is built and installed again with the new installation's wall-panel address; until then, a panel keeps asking for its data and shows that no current data arrives. With Delete everything, a new installation imports only the readings that Home Assistant's recorder still holds (10 days by default). Home Assistant's Delete has no options, so what it keeps is chosen beforehand: {screen_report} > When GlucoCraft is deleted, Keep the readings for a reinstall (the default) or Delete everything. Reload in the same menu restarts GlucoCraft without deleting anything; Disable turns it off. With Keep the readings for a reinstall, the stored readings, the laboratory A1C results and the sensor changes are kept in the folder glucocraft/; the settings are not kept, so a reinstall starts with the default settings; and everything else listed below is removed; the notification GlucoCraft deleted says where they are. A new installation asks whether to keep them or to delete them and start fresh; deleting that folder also deletes them. With Delete everything, deleting GlucoCraft removes every file GlucoCraft stored in the Home Assistant configuration (the readings in glucocraft/, including copies of a damaged file, every CSV export in glucocraft_exports/ and every report PDF in glucocraft_reports/, and these folders when they are empty), GlucoCraft's stores in .storage (state, laboratory A1C results, sensor events, panels already announced), its Repairs issues and notifications, the recorded history and long-term statistics of the entities it has at that moment in Home Assistant's recorder, the GlucoCraft dashboard and the card resources. Home Assistant removes the entities and the device. When it removes the entities, its recorder records each removal as one empty state (without a value), which it removes after its recorder period. The entities of an optional feature that was turned off earlier no longer exist, so their history is not removed: Home Assistant removes their recorded states after its recorder period, and their long-term statistics can be removed in Developer tools > Statistics, or with the rest when the feature is turned on again before GlucoCraft is deleted. Copies in Home Assistant backups and in downloaded or shared files, messages already sent to phones and lines in Home Assistant's log are not affected. CSV exports copied out of glucocraft_exports/ before GlucoCraft was deleted can be read back in after a reinstall (the action glucocraft.import_csv, {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}).

• What Home Assistant keeps. Besides the empty states and the statistics named above, Home Assistant keeps its own records: the removed entities and the device stay in the lists of deleted items of its entity and device registries (used when they are added again); its list of dashboard resources (.storage/lovelace_resources), created when GlucoCraft registered its card files, stays, without GlucoCraft's entries; and the reportlab package that Home Assistant installed for GlucoCraft's PDF stays installed. None of these holds a glucose value.
docs.section.setup.title: Setup
docs.section.setup.body:
The setup asks, in this order: the disclaimer (GlucoCraft Disclaimer); what to do with the readings of an earlier installation (only when there are any); Glucose Sources (the source, the CGM sensor expiry entity, the sensor limits, the second source and No current data after); and Units and Notifications (the display unit, the daily summary and its time, the dashboard in the sidebar and the phones). Every other setting starts at its default.

After the setup, Settings Status and Maintenance show:
<ul>
• the unit of the source (mg/dL or mmol/L);
• the reading interval of the source (designed for 5 minutes or more often);
• the sensor lower and upper limits in use (the measurement ranges of common CGM systems: see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)});
• the Maintenance status: No issues, or the issues to resolve, such as a source that updates too slowly or a sensor limit that does not match.
<ul>

• Location. {configure} (the gear icon on the GlucoCraft row); the Change Settings button on Settings Status opens GlucoCraft in Settings > Devices & services, where Configure is selected. A menu lists the screens by topic: {screen_sources}, {screen_units}, Optional features, Glucose ranges and Custom goals (these two only while Custom ranges and goals is on), {screen_displays}, {screen_notifications} and {screen_report}. Each field has a short label with an explanation under it; the second source and the graph range colors are collapsed sections that open when selected. Submit saves that screen only and reloads GlucoCraft, whose entities are unavailable while it reloads; ✕ closes a screen without saving. Settings Status lists the values in use and the requirements of each setting. Each setting below names its screen.

• Glucose source ({screen_sources}). A Home Assistant sensor entity whose state is the glucose value in mg/dL or mmol/L (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Readings), selected at first setup. The Second glucose source is optional. A second source is designed to supply readings that the primary source misses, up to 24 hours back, and to continue when it stops, merged by measurement time (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Two sources). {interval_note}

• Sensor lower limit and sensor upper limit (each source; {screen_sources}). Automatic or the limits of the CGM system's measurement range (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}). With the lower limit set by hand, a reading at or below it is LO; with Automatic, only a reading below it. With the upper limit set by hand, a reading at or above it is HI; with Automatic, only a reading above it. A change applies to readings received after it; stored readings are not changed. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. {limit_note}

• Display unit ({screen_units}; at setup, the last screen). mg/dL or mmol/L for every value shown on the dashboard, the display card, the wall panels, the report and in notifications; the default is the source entity's unit. The ranges in the settings are entered in this unit.

• Time format and date format ({screen_units}). Time format: Automatic, 12-hour (7:46 AM) or 24-hour (07:46, with a leading zero). Date format: Automatic, month-day-year (10/22/2026), day-month-year (22/10/2026) or year-month-day (2026-10-22). Used on the dashboard, the display card, the wall panels and in the report and PDF. Automatic (the default) follows Home Assistant's country: for example 12-hour and month-day-year in the United States, 24-hour and day-month-year in most of Europe. Home Assistant's own time and date settings belong to each user's profile and cannot be read by the panels or the PDF; GlucoCraft therefore has its own. Weekday and month names are in English.

• First day of the week, decimal separator, A1C and GMI unit ({screen_units}) and PDF paper size ({screen_report}). Each is Automatic (the default) or a choice, like the time and date formats. First day of the week: Monday, Sunday or Saturday; Automatic follows Home Assistant's country (without a country: Sunday); used where calendar weeks are shown (the CGM Report page and its PDF); rolling 7-day periods remain rolling. Decimal separator: point (3.9) or comma (3,9); Automatic follows Home Assistant's country, and in Canada and Switzerland, or without a country, Home Assistant's language; every decimal shown on the dashboard, the display card, the wall panels, the report and PDF and in notifications; stored data, attributes and the HTTP API always use a point. A1C and GMI unit: % (6.5%), mmol/mol (48 mmol/mol) or both (6.5% (48 mmol/mol)), for GMI and laboratory A1C; Automatic follows Home Assistant's country: mmol/mol where laboratories report IFCC units only, both units where they report both, and percent elsewhere; without a country, both units with the display unit mmol/L and percent with mg/dL. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. {gmi_mmol_rule} PDF paper size: Letter or A4; Automatic uses Letter in the United States and its territories, Canada, Mexico, the Philippines and the Letter countries of Latin America, and without a country; A4 elsewhere. The settings in use are listed on Settings Status.

• Summaries ({screen_notifications}). Daily summary (on by default) and Daily summary time (default 08:00); Weekly summary (off by default) and Weekly summary day (default Sunday); the monthly summary is sent with the weekly summary. See {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}. No-data notice (off by default) and Notify after (default 30 minutes): see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}.

• Phones (optional; {screen_notifications}; at setup, the last screen). Also send notifications to: the phones and other notify actions that also receive GlucoCraft's notifications (none selected: the notifications stay in Home Assistant); Notifications to send there: the notification types they receive; Send a test notification now: one test message. See {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}, Phones.

• Display card layout ({screen_displays}). The card on the Start page, chosen independently of the wall panels: Square (480 × 480, the layout of the square example panel, Guition 480 × 480; the default) or Rectangular (800 × 480, the layout of the 800 × 480 example panel, and close to the 1024 × 600 and 480 × 320 ones). Both show the same pages; a card that does not match a panel shows the same information in a different layout. The last page of every card and panel is the About page, About GlucoCraft (page 17 of 17 on the display card): GlucoCraft's icon, the {sec:disclaimer|Disclaimer}, the version and the copyright line. The two display cards can also be added to other dashboards (in the dashboard editor: Add card, then a GlucoCraft Display Card); a card added there keeps its own layout, which this setting does not change. When a wall panel is connected for the first time, a notification names its shape and the card in use; the panel appears in the panel list on Maintenance after the dashboard page is reloaded.

• Trend shown as ({screen_displays}). Arrow (the default): one arrow in the TREND column, turned by the rate of change. Word: the trend word in its place (for example Falling quickly; a longer word on two lines), the broader category of the same rate. Either way the zone word is shown under the glucose value (Very low, Low, In range, Tight range, High, Very high), so that the range does not depend on color alone, the value keeps its range color, the 5-minute delta is shown, and the screen-reader description reads both the zone and the trend. The trend is not shown while there is no current data, during a sensor warm-up or while the trend is unknown; after the stated sensor expiry, while readings still arrive, it follows the data. The small value in the corner of the square wall panel's weekly pages shows the trend as the arrow with either choice.

• Display colors ({screen_displays}). One color for each of the seven ranges (very low, low, in range below the tight range, tight range, in range above the tight range, high, very high), used for the glucose value on the display card and the wall panels; the default palette shows lows in red and highs in blue, and Restore the default palette returns to it. A second set of seven colors, Graph range colors (a collapsed section), is used for the range bands of the graphs (the display card, the wall panels and the dashboard's graphs), by default the time-in-ranges colors of the CGM Report, with its own restore option (Restore the default graph colors). The background of the display card (the Home Assistant theme or a color) and the background of the wall panels (a color) are set on the same screen, black by default; the text is black or white, whichever has the higher contrast with the background, and the graphs stay on black. The description at the top of the screen states the measured contrast of the saved colors on the saved background, and of the graphs' white labels on each graph range color. Outline text (off by default) draws a thin 1-pixel edge around the graph labels and the text drawn in a range color on the display card and the wall panels, for light backgrounds and light graph bands. The zone word remains with any colors (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors} and {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}). The CGM Report keeps the colors of the published report examples.

• Fade the words when there is no current reading ({screen_displays}; on by default). While there is no current reading, the words Sensor warming up, Sensor expired or No current data, shown in place of the value, fade to about 30% brightness and back every 3 seconds for the first 30 minutes of each episode, and the status bar's Sensor expiry passed for as long as the stated expiry has passed; off, both stay still (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).

• Range set of the weekly pages ({screen_displays}). The consensus ranges with the consensus targets (the default) or the custom ranges with the custom goals, for the weekly pages of the display card and every wall panel together; offered only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on and custom ranges or goals are set (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• Measurement-time attribute (optional; not at setup; {screen_sources}, for the primary source and in the section Second glucose source). The attribute of a source entity containing the measurement time, where it is not recognized automatically.

• CGM sensor expiry entity (optional; {screen_sources}). An entity whose state is the sensor's expiry (date and time, date or time stamp) or the time remaining with a unit (days, hours or minutes). Without it, expiry and expiry-based warm-up detection are not available. After the stated expiry the status shows Sensor expired in red; while readings still arrive, the value keeps its zone color, the trend follows the readings, and the status bar shows Sensor expiry passed (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Sensor expiry, which also lists the Repairs notices about this entity).

• Optional features (Optional features). Two switches, each off in a new installation; the setup does not ask for them. Custom ranges and goals: on, the ranges and goals in the settings are used for the zone of the glucose value on the display card and the wall panels (its color and its zone word), the range bands of the graphs and the statistics under the graphs on the display card and the wall panels and, where selected, the weekly pages; it adds the page Custom Ranges, the CGM Report's appendix Custom Ranges and Goals, the screens Glucose ranges and Custom goals and, per period, the custom ranges entity and the six custom time-in-band entities. The range binary sensors (Glucose below range, Glucose above range, Glucose very low, Glucose very high, Glucose in range and Glucose in tight range), the zone attribute of the Last glucose reading sensor and the zone in the Spoken summary use the same ranges, so turning the feature on or off also changes these entities. Where the custom ranges differ from the consensus ranges, GlucoCraft calculates the statistics of every period twice, on the custom and on the consensus ranges, every 5 minutes. Off, the consensus ranges and targets are used everywhere {cite:battelino2019} with the tight range {cite:battelino2023}, and the stored ranges and goals are kept for when the switch is turned on again. Separate statistics entities: on, one entity per statistic and period for the mean, standard deviation, CV, lowest and highest reading, readings and sensor active, and for the GMI and the GRI of the periods of 14 days and longer (57 entities), available to other dashboards, automations and scripts like any Home Assistant entity; off, these entities are not created. The dashboard, the display card and the wall panels never use them: the same values are attributes of each period's consensus ranges entity (see {sec:entities|Entity Names}). Turning a switch off removes its entities from Home Assistant; changes made to these entities in Home Assistant (entity ID, name, area, labels, hidden or disabled) are not kept. Home Assistant keeps their recorded states for its recorder period and their long-term statistics; turning the switch on again creates the entities under GlucoCraft's own identifiers, and their history continues. Home Assistant's recorder stores a row for every change of a GlucoCraft entity's state or attributes; measured over one simulated day on Home Assistant 2026.10.4 with 200 days of readings stored: with a reading every minute, about 10,000 rows with both switches off and about 20,000 with both on (with a second source and custom ranges); with a reading every 5 minutes, about 3,900 and 14,000.

• Ranges and goals (screens Glucose ranges and Custom goals, while Custom ranges and goals is on). The default ranges are the consensus ranges {cite:battelino2019} with the tight range {cite:battelino2023}; the other default goals are the consensus targets {cite:battelino2019,monnier2017}. {no_default_goals} {custom_note} The very-low limit cannot be lower than the glucose sensor's lower limit and the very-high limit not higher than its upper limit (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}). The values are entered in the display unit and must be in ascending order: very low less than low, low at most tight range from, tight range from less than tight range to, tight range to at most high, and high less than very high; a value out of order is marked at its field. Each goal is compared as its label states: time in range more than the goal; time in tight range at least the goal; the times below and above the limits and GMI less than the goal; CV at most the goal. Changes take effect immediately on the display card and wall panels, and on Custom Ranges within 5 minutes; the consensus pages are not affected.
• No current data after ({screen_sources}; 5 to 30 minutes, default 15 minutes; why, and what the screens then show: see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).

• Report printer (optional; {screen_report}). The address of a network printer that accepts PDF over the Internet Printing Protocol (IPP): a host, or an ipp://, ipps://, http:// or https:// address, without a user name or password, for example ipp://192.0.2.10; without a port, 631 is used, and without a path, /ipp/print (see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).

• Wall panels (optional; {screen_displays}). Needed only if wall panels are used. Create a new wall-panel address creates the address from which the panels read their data; the address and its id are shown at the top of that screen, to administrators only. No address exists after the setup: if a wall panel is to be built, the box is ticked once to create the first address before that panel is built, because the build needs its id. After that, a new address is created only if the address may have been exposed, for example in a shared log, backup or screenshot; it is never a routine step. The moment a new address is created, the earlier one stops working, and every wall panel stops receiving data and shows that no current data arrives until each one is built and installed again with the new id, because the id is built into each panel's firmware (in the example panel configurations, from secrets.yaml). Creating or changing the wall-panel address: (1) on the screen {screen_displays}, tick Create a new wall-panel address and submit; (2) open the screen again and copy the id shown at the top; (3) enter it in each panel's configuration (in the example configurations: glucocraft_panel_webhook_id in secrets.yaml); (4) build and install every panel; (5) check that each panel shows current data.

• Dashboard in the sidebar ({screen_report}; at setup, the last screen). Shows the GlucoCraft dashboard, with this Documentation, in Home Assistant's sidebar; on by default. Off, the dashboard is removed; the GlucoCraft cards remain available for other dashboards.

• When GlucoCraft is deleted ({screen_report}). Keep the readings for a reinstall (the default): deleting GlucoCraft keeps the stored readings, the laboratory A1C results and the sensor changes for a new installation (not the settings: a reinstall starts with the default settings) and removes everything else; Delete everything: nothing of GlucoCraft's own is left behind. See {sec:install|Installing, Updating and Removing GlucoCraft}.
• History retained: the last {retention} days (a fixed period, not configurable); older readings are removed as whole days at local midnight (see {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}).
docs.section.cgms.title: Supported Sources
docs.section.cgms.body: GlucoCraft reads glucose values from entities that other integrations provide. It connects to no CGM system, device or cloud service itself, and it does not identify the CGM model. Reading frequency, delivery delay and the availability of measurement times depend on the integration and service that provide the data.

• Any glucose sensor entity. A Home Assistant sensor entity whose state is a glucose value in mg/dL or mmol/L, for example from an integration for the manufacturer's cloud service or for another CGM data service. Its unit, its measurement time and the states that are not readings are described in {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Readings. GlucoCraft's own entities cannot be chosen as sources.

• Measurement range. Readings outside the CGM system's measurement range are shown as LO or HI and give no value; the limits are set per source, and with Automatic three integrations are recognized and given their CGM systems' published limits (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}). {limit_note}

• A second source. Optional: a second entity, for example from a second system that reads the same CGM sensor, merged with the first by measurement time (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Readings). Each source has its own sensor limits and measurement-time attribute.

• Reading interval. {interval_note} A source whose readings arrive every 15 minutes or less often is not supported for live display, and a repair notice says so (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).
• How data are updated. GlucoCraft does not poll. It processes each new state of a source entity when Home Assistant reports it, and checks every minute whether the data are still current.

• Repeated values. A reading reaches GlucoCraft when the source entity writes a state, also one with an unchanged value. A source that writes no state when the value repeats (for example a template sensor, which Home Assistant updates only when the result of its template changes) delivers no reading for the repeated value: such readings are not stored, and the measured reading interval is longer than the CGM's. From a source without its own measurement time, an unchanged value written again counts as a new reading only once three quarters of the source's reading interval (at least 20 seconds) have passed since its last reading, so that a source that writes its state more often than it measures adds no extra readings. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.
  • A source without measurement times. A source without its own measurement time cannot tell GlucoCraft that it has stopped: if it keeps writing its last value, GlucoCraft shows that value as current. Where the source has an attribute with the time of each measurement, set it in the settings. The setting is Measurement-time attribute ({screen_sources}). After 12 identical readings in a row over at least 60 minutes from such a source, the repair notice Glucose source may have stopped: the same value for over an hour explains what to check; it closes by itself when the value changes. This method is a GlucoCraft rule.

GlucoCraft needs a new reading every 5 minutes or more often to show a current value. A source that delivers its readings less often, or hours late, is not supported for live display: its readings are stored and shown, but the trend, the 5-minute delta and No current data do not work as intended with it. These CGM systems cannot deliver that:

CGM systemWhyWhat worksWhat does not work
FreeStyle Libre 14 day, FreeStyle Libre (first generation)A new reading only when the sensor is scanned; stored values every 15 minutes {cite:abbott2021}Readings stored and shown; graphs, statistics and the CGM ReportTrend, 5-minute delta, the no-current-data limit, data gaps, sensor active
Dexcom SteloNo real-time sharing; readings reach other software about 3 hours late {cite:dexcomStelo}Graphs, statistics and the CGM Report, once the readings arriveEvery live display shows No current data; no trend or 5-minute delta
Abbott LingoReadings shared only about 3 hours late, and only within its sharing range {cite:stiehl2025}Graphs, statistics and the CGM Report, once the readings arrive, without the readings outside that rangeEvery live display shows No current data; no trend or 5-minute delta

GlucoCraft is built for readings from a CGM sensor. Readings from a blood glucose meter or entered by hand are stored and shown, but the statistics, the trend and the data-gap rules are not designed for them.
Readings passed on through a phone's health app are not supported for live display either:

Health appWhy
Apple Health (through the Home Assistant iOS app)No measurement time on the readings; no new readings while the iPhone is locked {cite:haSensors}; Dexcom readings arrive about 3 hours late {cite:dexcomSharing}
Health Connect (through the Home Assistant Android app)Readings every 15 minutes at the app's default update frequency {cite:haSensors}; Dexcom readings arrive about 3 hours late {cite:dexcomSharing}
With either, the features listed above do not work as described.

GlucoCraft is designed for every CGM system that delivers readings every 5 minutes or more often. If readings arrive every 15 minutes or less often for any reason, GlucoCraft shows a Repairs notice. Information as of October 2026.
docs.section.entities.title: Entity Names
docs.section.entities.body: All GlucoCraft entity identifiers begin with glucocraft_, and all display names with "GlucoCraft". They are ordinary Home Assistant entities (see {sec:automations|Automations}). In the display names the period is written 6H, 24H, 7D, 14D, 30D, 90D and 180D (6 hours to 180 days); CV, GMI and GRI are the coefficient of variation, the glucose management indicator and the Glycemia Risk Index (see {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}).

GlucoCraft keeps its entity identifiers. This dashboard, GlucoCraft cards and wall panels refer to these identifiers, and those of a wall panel are built into its firmware, so they must stay the same for GlucoCraft to continue to function properly. Home Assistant has no way to lock an identifier, so when one is changed while GlucoCraft is running, GlucoCraft gives the original back within seconds and says so in the repair notice GlucoCraft put its entity ids back. This also covers a new name for the GlucoCraft device, when Home Assistant changes the identifiers with it. Names can be changed freely: to change a label, change the entity's display name (Settings > Devices & services > Entities > the entity > Name) or the name of the device. If Home Assistant offers to change the entity identifiers as well, leave them as they are. For a change GlucoCraft could not undo, see {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}.
Default entities. Created in every installation and enabled.
<table>
<tr><th>Entity</th><th>Content</th></tr>

sensor.glucocraft_last_glucose_readingMost recent reading, in the display unit (in mmol/L, Home Assistant shows it rounded, and an automation reading the state sees all its decimals: the attribute value_mgdl gives the value in mg/dL); unknown during a limit reading; attributes zone (very_low, low, near_low, tight_range, near_high, high, very_high), zone_color, value_mgdl (the value in mg/dL; during a limit reading the stored limit, which is no measurement), unit (the display unit), limit (low, high or none: a reading outside the sensor's range, which gives no value) and limit_text (LO, HI or none), zone_label (the zone word outside the range, none in range), display_word (the zone word the displays show under the value; Sensor limit during a limit reading), and, for the LO / HI screen, limit_since (the start of the current run of limit readings, none outside a run), last_measured_mgdl and last_measured_ts (the newest measured reading before the run, in mg/dL, and its time).

sensor.glucocraft_last_reading_timeMeasurement time of the most recent reading; attribute time_untrusted, on while that time is more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock (the displays then show Reading: ---).

sensor.glucocraft_statusStatus: Current data, No current data, Sensor expiring soon, Sensor expired, Sensor warming up or No data yet, in this order of priority: warm-up, expired, no data yet, no current data, expiring soon, current data. Attributes label (the status name) and color (#43A047 current data; #F9A825 sensor expiring soon; #E53935 sensor expired and no current data; #7E57C2 sensor warming up and no data yet).
sensor.glucocraft_active_sourceSource of the current value; attribute second_source_active indicates the second source.

sensor.glucocraft_trend_arrowTrend arrow (TREND on the display card and wall panels); attributes description (the trend category; Unknown while no trend is known), word (the trend word shown with the setting Trend shown as: Word; empty while no trend is known), angle (the angle of the arrow on the display card and the wall panels) and source (the citation of the trend categories).
sensor.glucocraft_5_minute_delta5-minute delta: the change of the smoothed glucose over 5 minutes, in the display unit; attribute value_mgdl.

sensor.glucocraft_data_historyThe span from the first to the last stored reading, as the longest statistics period it reaches (No data, Less than 6 hours, 6 hours … 180 days); not the share of time with data, which is Sensor active. Attribute storage_problem: save_failed while the readings file cannot be written, or recovered, damaged, unreadable or newer after a problem with the readings file (see {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}).

sensor.glucocraft_sensor_expiryNot expired, Expiring soon (24 hours or less), Expired, Not configured (no expiry entity), No value (the expiry entity has no value) or Unknown format (its value is not recognized); attributes expiry_entity, expiry_format, expires_at, remaining_hours, remaining_days and expiry_value (the expiry entity's own state).
binary_sensor.glucocraft_no_current_dataOn: no current data.
binary_sensor.glucocraft_sensor_warm_upOn: sensor warm-up in progress.
binary_sensor.glucocraft_glucose_below_rangeOn: the glucose is below range (the ranges in use); unknown while there is no current data.
binary_sensor.glucocraft_using_custom_rangesOn: custom ranges are in use; always off while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is off.

sensor.glucocraft_<period>_consensus_rangesState: the time in range, 70–180 mg/dL (3.9–10.0 mmol/L), in percent; attributes: every statistic of the period with the consensus ranges, including limit_readings (the number of LO and HI readings, low and high) and limit_seconds (the seconds they represent), and the enough-data rule's facts enough_data, period_seconds and covered_seconds; without enough data the state and every statistic are empty; a period without any reading has only the attribute has_data (false).

sensor.glucocraft_weekly_statisticsThe 7-day values of the last 26 weeks (attribute weeks; the GMI of a week is the 14-day GMI at the week's end (calculated hourly, with Change Over Time), and a week without enough data, less than 70% sensor active, has no values) and the 4-week direction of each weekly page on the consensus ranges, from the 14-day values (attribute directions; with Range set of the weekly pages set to the custom ranges, the weekly pages show the directions of the custom ranges). This method is a GlucoCraft rule. Attribute computed_at: the time the statistics were last calculated (every 5 minutes).
sensor.glucocraft_change_over_timeChange Over Time for both range sets (attributes consensus, custom): the 14-day and 7-day values of the last 26 weeks and the 4-week comparison periods.

sensor.glucocraft_configurationAll settings in use (attributes), including gap_threshold_seconds and reading_interval_seconds (the source in use), retention_days and, per source under sources, lower_limit / upper_limit (mg/dL, in use) with their settings, trend_display (the setting Trend shown as: arrow or word) maintenance_issues (the Maintenance status: one entry per issue, read by the Maintenance button and the Maintenance issues card) and attention (on while a GlucoCraft Repairs notice is open and not ignored: Check Home Assistant on the displays).

Entities that start disabled. Created in every installation but disabled, because no GlucoCraft page, card or panel reads them. Each is enabled on its own: Settings > Devices & services > Entities > the entity > the gear > Enabled, then Update.

<tr><th>Entity</th><th>Content</th></tr>

binary_sensor.glucocraft_glucose_above_range, _glucose_very_low, _glucose_very_high, _glucose_in_range and _glucose_in_tight_rangeOn: the glucose is above range, very low, very high, in range or in the tight range (the ranges in use); unknown while there is no current data.

Entities of the optional features. Created only while their optional feature is on; both are off in a new installation. A feature is turned on at {configure} > Optional features. Turning it off removes its entities; their recorded history stays.
<table>
<tr><th>Entity</th><th>Content</th></tr>
sensor.glucocraft_<period>_custom_rangesAll statistics of a period with the ranges in the settings (attributes), only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on.

sensor.glucocraft_<period>_custom_time_in_range and the other custom timesOne time in a range per entity, with the ranges in the settings, for each period, only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on: _custom_time_in_range, _custom_time_in_tight_range, _custom_time_low, _custom_time_high, _custom_time_very_low and _custom_time_very_high. _custom_time_low and _custom_time_high are level 1 only (from the very-low limit up to the low limit, and from the high limit up to the very-high limit); all the time below the low limit and above the high limit, levels 1 and 2 together, is in the attributes time_below_low and time_above_high of _custom_ranges.
