The complete list of entities and attributes is in the file docs/ENTITIES_AND_API.md of GlucoCraft's repository, https://github.com/Verstreubulator/glucocraft. The HTTP API (/api/glucocraft/...) requires a Home Assistant login; it serves the cards and the report page.
docs.section.glossary.title: Glossary
docs.section.glossary.body: The terms below are used on this dashboard, in the report and its PDF, on the display card and on the wall panels. Wall panels are optional; where this Documentation describes them, it describes panels built from the example panel configurations. Home Assistant terms (integration, entity, attribute, Repairs and others) have their usual meaning; see the Home Assistant documentation.
<ul>

• 14-day values (weekly pages). The values of the 14 days ending at each of the last 26 week ends, counted back from the present time; the weekly pages and Change Over Time show them, because 14 days is the period the 2019 consensus recommends {cite:battelino2019}. A week with less than 70% sensor active is shown as a gap. This method is a GlucoCraft rule (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• A1C (HbA1c). Glycated hemoglobin, a laboratory blood test. A1C "reflects average glycemia over approximately 2–3 months" {cite:ada2026|Glycemic Assessment by A1C section, para. 1}. It is reported in percent (NGSP) or in mmol/mol (IFCC).

• Ambulatory Glucose Profile (AGP). A standardized report of CGM data, recommended by an expert panel {cite:bergenstal2013}; the abbreviation AGP appears in the titles of cited works. The CGM Report shows the standardized metrics and glucose profile recommended for the Ambulatory Glucose Profile {cite:battelino2019,bergenstal2013} (see CGM Report).

• Appendix (CGM Report). An optional part at the end of the CGM Report, off by default: Custom Ranges and Goals, the statistics with the ranges and goals in the settings (only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on), and Measures Defined for Research, measures that the 2023 consensus defines for clinical trials, shown without targets {cite:battelino2023} (see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).

• Automatic (setting value). The default value of several settings, which GlucoCraft takes from the source or from Home Assistant instead of a fixed choice: the sensor lower and upper limit from what the source shows and the integration that delivers it (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}); the time format, the date format, the first day of the week, the decimal separator, the A1C and GMI unit and the PDF paper size from Home Assistant's country or language (see {sec:setup|Setup}).

• Background (display card, wall panels). The color behind the text of the display card (the Home Assistant theme or a chosen color) and of the wall panels (a chosen color), black by default ({screen_displays}). The text is black or white, whichever contrasts more with the background; the graphs always keep their black area (see {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}).
• Blood glucose meter (finger stick). A handheld device that measures glucose in a drop of blood from the fingertip.

• CGM (continuous glucose monitoring); CGM system. A wearable sensor measures glucose in the interstitial fluid under the skin at regular intervals and sends the readings to its own app, reader or receiver. The CGM system is the sensor together with that app, reader or receiver and its alarms. Glucose in the interstitial fluid follows blood glucose with a delay; the Standards of Care mention this "lag time between interstitial glucose and venous glucose" {cite:ada2025|p. S130}.

• CGM Report. GlucoCraft's report page and its PDF. The CGM Report shows the standardized metrics and glucose profile recommended for the Ambulatory Glucose Profile {cite:battelino2019,bergenstal2013}. The CGM Report and its PDF can be printed or shared, for example with a healthcare professional. Its main sections use the consensus ranges only; the optional appendix Custom Ranges and Goals, only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on, shows the statistics with the ranges and goals in the settings (see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).

• Clinical care and clinical trials. Clinical care is the diabetes care that individuals receive from their healthcare team. Clinical trials are research studies of treatments. The 2019 consensus sets clinical targets for CGM data interpretation {cite:battelino2019}; the 2023 consensus states that CGM metrics should be considered "for use in all clinical studies in diabetes" {cite:battelino2023|p. 42}, and some of its definitions differ (for example, when a level 2 event ends).

• Consensus (consensus statement). A published statement in which a panel, convened for that purpose, agrees on definitions, ranges and targets. GlucoCraft's ranges and targets come from three: the international consensus on the use of continuous glucose monitoring {cite:danne2017}, the International Consensus on Time in Range for clinical care {cite:battelino2019}, and the international consensus statement on CGM metrics for clinical trials {cite:battelino2023}. The panels of 2017 and 2019 were international panels of physicians, researchers and individuals with diabetes {cite:battelino2019,danne2017}. GlucoCraft also cites a consensus report on the definition of remission {cite:riddle2021} and a joint position statement {cite:ihsg2017}. Individual studies and manufacturer documents are named as such and are not called consensus.

• Consensus ranges; custom ranges; range set. The two sets of ranges. The consensus ranges are those of the cited consensus statements {cite:battelino2019} with the tight range {cite:battelino2023} and cannot be changed. The custom ranges are those in the settings; by default they equal the consensus ranges. The pages Consensus Ranges and Custom Ranges show the statistics calculated with each set; Custom Ranges exists only while the optional feature Custom ranges and goals is on. The weekly pages of the display card and wall panels use one of two range sets: the consensus ranges or the custom ranges (setting Range set of the weekly pages; see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• Core measures. The measures shown first on Consensus Ranges and, while it exists, Custom Ranges, for the last 14 days, each with its consensus target or custom goal and its change over time: time in range, time in tight range, the time below the low and the very-low limit, and the time above the high limit (see {sec:pages|Pages}).

• CSV (comma-separated values). A plain-text table format, one row per line, with the columns separated by commas, which spreadsheet and other programs can read. GlucoCraft's export uses it (see {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}).

• Custom goal. A value for a metric set by the user in GlucoCraft's settings (screen Custom goals), compared with the statistics on Custom Ranges and on the weekly pages with the custom range set. The goals start at the consensus targets {cite:battelino2019,monnier2017}; the goals for time in tight range and for GMI have no default value.

• DCCT; EDIC; UKPDS. Names of cited studies: the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) and its follow-up, the Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC) study {cite:nathan2014}; UKPDS is the name of the study whose observational analysis is cited {cite:stratton2000} (see {sec:studies|Published Findings}).

• Delivery test. The message GlucoCraft delivery test, sent once to the phones and other notify actions selected in the settings with Send a test notification now ({screen_notifications}); its arrival does not show that later messages will arrive (see {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}).

• Diagnostics file. A file that Home Assistant offers for an integration (Settings > Devices & services > GlucoCraft, the menu with three dots, Download diagnostics) for looking into a problem. GlucoCraft's file contains its settings and the state of its sources, but no glucose value, and no custom range limits or goals (see {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}).

• Display card. GlucoCraft's dashboard card, which shows the current value, the trend and the graphs on 17 pages in one of two layouts, each that of a wall-panel shape: square or rectangular (setting Display card layout; see {sec:setup|Setup}).

• Display colors; graph range colors. Two sets of colors in the settings ({screen_displays}), one color for each range from very low to very high. The display colors color the glucose value on the display card and the wall panels; the graph range colors color the range bands of the graphs (the display card, the wall panels and the dashboard's graphs), by default the colors of the CGM Report's time in ranges. Each set has its own restore option (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• Example panel configurations. The panel configurations are examples. They are not a finished or ready-to-use product. The user's own ESPHome builds the firmware (the program on the panel) from them.

• Extended high-glucose event. A period in which sensor glucose stays above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) for at least 120 minutes, ending when glucose has returned to 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) or below for 15 minutes {cite:battelino2023|p. 48}. A measure defined for clinical trials, shown only in the optional research appendix of the CGM Report, without a target (see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).
• GlucoCraft rule. A method chosen by GlucoCraft where no cited source defines one, for example the gap rule or the 4-week direction. Every GlucoCraft rule is labeled as such where it is used.
• Glycemic variability. How much glucose rises and falls over a period. The 2017 consensus designates the coefficient of variation (CV) as the primary measure of variability {cite:danne2017}.
• GRI components (hypo, hyper). The hypoglycemia and the hyperglycemia component of the Glycemia Risk Index {cite:klonoff2023}, defined in {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}.

• Hazard ratio; odds; R²; r. Statistical terms of the published findings. A hazard ratio compares the rate at which an event occurs over time in one group with the rate in another group (1.83: an 83% higher rate). Odds compare how often an event occurs with how often it does not. R² (from 0 to 1) states how much of the variation of one value another value explains; r (from −1 to 1) states how closely two values vary together. They describe study populations, not an individual (see {sec:studies|Published Findings}).
• Healthcare team. The clinicians who provide a person's diabetes care, for example a physician, a nurse, a diabetes educator or a dietitian.
• Hyperglycemia, levels 1 and 2. In the consensus metrics, level 1 is 181–250 mg/dL (10.1–13.9 mmol/L) and level 2 is above 250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L) {cite:battelino2019}.

• Hypoglycemia, levels 1 to 3. Level 1 is a glucose concentration below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) and at or above 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L). Level 2 is below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L). Level 3 is "a severe event characterized by altered mental and/or physical status requiring assistance for treatment of hypoglycemia, irrespective of glucose level" {cite:ada2025|Table 6.4}. CGM data can show levels 1 and 2; level 3 is not a glucose value, and GlucoCraft does not show it. Levels 1 and 2 are the same in the 2019 consensus {cite:battelino2019}.

• Increasing; decreasing; stable. The words of the 4-week direction on the weekly pages of the display card and the wall panels: the mean of the weekly 14-day values of the last 4 weeks compared with the mean of the 4 weeks before (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• IPP (Internet Printing Protocol). The standard network protocol through which GlucoCraft sends the PDF of the CGM Report to a printer, on port 631 unless the printer address names another port (setting Report printer; see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).

• Limit reading (LO / HI). A reading below or above the CGM sensor's measurement range, which the CGM system reports as a text such as LO or HI, or as a code, instead of a number; with a sensor lower or upper limit set by hand, also a reading at that limit. GlucoCraft shows it as LO or HI, leaves it out of every calculated value and counts it as very low or very high in the time in ranges; on the graphs, small marks along the bottom or the top edge show when such readings were received. This method is a GlucoCraft rule (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}).

• Maintenance status. The state on the Maintenance button of the Start page and on the Maintenance page: No issues, or the number of issues to resolve, such as an offline wall panel, an open repair notice or a failed CSV export (see {sec:pages|Pages}).
• Manufacturer documentation. Information published by the maker of a CGM system, such as the meaning of the trend arrows or the measurement range of a sensor.
• Mean; standard deviation (SD). The mean is the time-weighted average of the readings. The standard deviation measures how widely the readings spread around the mean, in the display unit.

• Median; percentile; interquartile range; 5–95% range. These describe the glucose profile of the CGM Report, which shows the percentiles 5, 25, 50, 75 and 95 of the readings by time of day. The median is the value below which half of the readings at that time of day lie. A percentile is the value below which that percentage of the readings lies. The interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile) contains the middle half of the readings. The 5–95% range contains all but the lowest and the highest 5%.
• mg/dL and mmol/L. Two units of glucose concentration: milligrams per deciliter and millimoles per liter; conversion and rounding: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Unit.

• NGSP; IFCC; mmol/mol. The National Glycohemoglobin Standardization Program {cite:ada2025} (results in %) and the International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (results in mmol/mol). The two scales are converted with the IFCC–NGSP master equation {cite:hoelzel2004}.

• Night and day (CGM Report). The two time blocks of the report's Hypoglycemia and Hyperglycemia tables: night, 00:00 to 05:59, and day, 06:00 to 23:59, as in the cited consensus statements ({ref:battelino2023}, Panel 2; {ref:danne2017}, Section 7) (see {sec:pages|Pages}, Report and PDF).

• No-data notice. An optional Home Assistant notification, off by default, that GlucoCraft has received no readings since a given time (setting Notify after); it is never about glucose (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).

• Optional features. Two switches in the settings (screen Optional features), both off in a new installation. Custom ranges and goals uses the ranges and goals in the settings for the displays, the page Custom Ranges and the CGM Report's custom appendix; while it is off, the consensus ranges and targets are used everywhere. Separate statistics entities creates one entity per statistic and period (see {sec:setup|Setup}).

• Outline text. A thin edge around the graph labels, the glucose value and the other text drawn in a zone color on the display card and the wall panels (setting Outline text, off by default), intended for light backgrounds and light graph bands (see {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}).

• Percentage point. The arithmetic difference between two percentages: a time in range of 75% instead of 70% is 5 percentage points higher (about 7% of the earlier value). Changes of time in range and differences between laboratory A1C and GMI are stated in percentage points.

• Period labels (6h, 24h, 7d, 14d, 30d, 90d, 180d). The rolling periods in entity names and identifiers (for example 14D consensus ranges, sensor.glucocraft_14d_consensus_ranges) and in the GMI labels of the display card and the wall panels (GMI14d): 6 and 24 hours, and 7, 14, 30, 90 and 180 days, each ending at the present time; 180 days is the period called 6 months on the dashboard (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}).

• Previous period (CGM Report). The period of the same length immediately before the report period, compared with it in the 14-day, 30-day and 90-day reports; the 6-month report has none (see {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}).
• Range. A band of glucose values, for example in range, 70–180 mg/dL (3.9–10.0 mmol/L).
• Reading. One glucose value with its measurement time, as delivered by the source.

• Short labels of the display card and wall panels. Statistics under each graph (the period of the page, with the ranges in use): TIR, time in range; TITR, time in tight range; Low and High, time in level 1 below and above the range; Very low and Very high, time in level 2 below and above the range; Avg, the time-weighted mean glucose; SD, standard deviation; CV, coefficient of variation; GMI14d, GMI30d, GMI90d and GMI180d, the glucose management indicator of the last 14, 30, 90 or 180 days (the 6-hour, 24-hour and 7-day pages show GMI14d, because GMI is calculated only for 14 days or more {cite:battelino2019,bergenstal2018}); Min and Max, the lowest and the highest measured reading; ---, no value (no readings in the period, less than 70% sensor active or, for GMI, less than 14 days). Glucose block: TREND, the trend arrow; 5 MIN DELTA, the 5-minute delta. Status bar: Reading: 3 min ago, the age of the newest reading, in whole minutes up to 99 and then in whole hours (Reading: 2 h ago); Warm-up: 12 min, the time since a sensor warm-up was recognized; Custom ranges, the ranges in use differ from the consensus ranges; Check Home Assistant, a GlucoCraft notice is open in Home Assistant's Repairs; Reading: ---, no reading yet, or a reading time more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock; Sensor Exp: 3d 4h, the time until the stated sensor expiry (Exp, expiry); Sensor expiry passed, the stated expiry has passed; d, h and m, days, hours and minutes; min and h in Reading: 3 min ago, minutes and hours. Graph key of the graphs of 24 hours and longer: --- Min to max, the area from the lowest to the highest reading of each time slot; --- Mean, the line of the mean of the readings in each slot (see {sec:privacy|Privacy and Wall Panels}). For lack of room the display card and the wall panels use the short forms Min, Max and Avg consistently (also in the weekly page Weekly: Min and Max); the dashboard and the CGM Report write Lowest, Highest and Mean, and the screen-reader texts say the words.

• Source; second source (optional). The Home Assistant sensor entity that delivers readings to GlucoCraft, for example from an integration for a CGM manufacturer's cloud service (see {sec:cgms|Supported Sources}). A second source is designed to supply readings that the primary source misses, up to 24 hours back, and to continue when it stops, merged by measurement time.

• Spoken summary. The entity sensor.glucocraft_spoken_summary, disabled by default: one ready-to-speak sentence with the data status, the value, its range, the time of the reading and the trend. See {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}, Voice.

• Standards of Care (ADA). The American Diabetes Association's (ADA) Standards of Care in Diabetes, updated every year. GlucoCraft cites Section 6, "Glycemic Goals and Hypoglycemia" {cite:ada2025}, the 2026 edition of that section {cite:ada2026}, and Section 7 of the 2026 edition, "Diabetes Technology" {cite:ada2026b}. Further sections consulted and left out are listed in {sec:left-out|What GlucoCraft Leaves Out, and Why}.

• Status; status bar; banner. The status describes the data GlucoCraft has, not the glucose value: Current data, No current data, Sensor expiring soon, Sensor expired, Sensor warming up or No data yet. The status bar of the display card and the wall panels shows it with the age of the newest reading; on the dashboard, a banner states No Current Data, the expiry time (Sensor Expires ... at ...), Sensor Expired or Sensor Warming Up, Second Source in Use and Reading Times Ahead of the Clock (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}, Colors).

• Study; published finding. A single research publication, and what it reported for the people it studied. A finding describes that population. It is not a target, and it is not a statement about any individual (see {sec:studies|Published Findings}).
• Target (consensus target). A value for a metric that a cited consensus statement publishes, for example a time in range of more than 70% {cite:battelino2019}. It is labeled Consensus target.

• TBR; TAR. Time below range (TBR), the percentage of time below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), and time above range (TAR), the percentage of time above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) {cite:battelino2019}. GlucoCraft writes both in full (see {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}).

• TIR; TITR. Time in range (TIR), the percentage of time at 70–180 mg/dL (3.9–10.0 mmol/L) {cite:battelino2019}, and time in tight range (TITR), the percentage of time at 70–140 mg/dL (3.9–7.8 mmol/L) {cite:battelino2023}. The abbreviations are used where space is short: in tables, on the display card and on the wall panels (see {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}).

• Treatment standards. In GlucoCraft's documentation, the consensus statements for clinical care and the Standards of Care. GlucoCraft is designed to calculate its results by these standards. Newer research, including the 2023 consensus for clinical trials, is shown only as context.

• Trend category; trend word. The direction and speed of the glucose change, in five categories: Rising quickly, Rising, Changing slowly, Falling and Falling quickly (the Trend arrow entity writes them with capitals, for example Rising Quickly), taken from one manufacturer's trend arrows {cite:abbott|p. 11} and applied by GlucoCraft to its own rate of change. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. The trend word is shown in the TREND column instead of the arrow when the setting Trend shown as is Word; it is the broader category of the same rate (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}).

• Trend shown as. The setting that chooses how the display card and the wall panels show the trend in the TREND column: the arrow (the default) or the trend word. The zone word is under the glucose value with either choice (see {sec:setup|Setup}).

• Wall panel; webhook. A wall panel is a small ESPHome device with a screen that shows GlucoCraft's data. It downloads those data on the local network from a webhook: a private address inside Home Assistant that GlucoCraft creates for the panels (the wall-panel address); this download is plain HTTP, not encrypted, while the panel's ESPHome connection with Home Assistant is encrypted (see {sec:privacy|Privacy and Wall Panels}).

• Wall-panel address. The webhook address from which the wall panels read their data. No address exists after the setup: it is created in the settings with Create a new wall-panel address ({screen_displays}), before the first wall panel is built, and its id goes into each panel's configuration (in the example panel configurations: glucocraft_panel_webhook_id in secrets.yaml). A new address stops the earlier one at once (see {sec:setup|Setup}).

• Weekly pages. The nine pages of the display card and the wall panels that show the 14-day values of the last 26 weeks, one measure per page, with the 4-week direction. They use one range set, chosen in the settings (Range set of the weekly pages; see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• Zone; zone word. The zone is the range a reading falls in, one of seven: very low, low, in range below the tight range, tight range, in range above the tight range, high and very high (the ranges in use; see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}). The zone word names it under the glucose value, in every setting (Very low, Low, In range, Tight range, High, Very high), so that the range does not depend on color alone. No zone word is shown while there is no current data or during a sensor warm-up; after the stated sensor expiry, while readings still arrive, the value and the zone word look as they did before it, and the status bar shows the expiry.
Terms defined in other sections
<ul>
• Sensor active, data sufficiency and the 70% rule: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}; {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}.
• Reading interval, gap, no current data: {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}.
• LO / HI, sensor lower and upper limit: {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}.
• Raw and smoothed values, trend arrow, rate of change, 5-minute delta: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}; {sec:entities|Entity Names}.
• Rolling periods, calendar days, retention, CSV export: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}; {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}.
• Time in range, time below and above range, time in tight range, CV, GMI, GRI, hypoglycemia event: {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}.
• Met / not met, the colors, 4-week direction: {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}.
• Sensor warm-up and sensor expiry: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}.
• Display unit, time format, date format: {sec:setup|Setup}.
• Notifications and summaries: {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}.
• Time weighting, measurement time, measurement-time attribute, history import: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}.
• Sensor cap notice, limit reading: {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}.
• Change Over Time, Direction: {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}; {sec:pages|Pages}.
• Range set of the weekly pages, display colors, zone word: {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}.
• Diagnostics file and repair notices: {sec:troubleshooting|Troubleshooting}; {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}.
docs.section.privacy.title: Privacy and Wall Panels
docs.section.privacy.body: Privacy
<ul>

• GlucoCraft runs inside the user's Home Assistant. It sends no data to its authors or to any cloud service of its own, and its authors do not receive, store or have access to any data that GlucoCraft processes. Data leave Home Assistant only when the user chooses to send them: notifications to the phones and other notify actions selected in GlucoCraft's settings, each delivered by that action's own service; CGM Reports sent to the printer address set in GlucoCraft's settings, which can be any address, inside or outside the home network (a host alone, or an address that begins with ipp:// or http://, sends the report unencrypted); and files the user downloads, exports or shares, such as CSV exports and diagnostics files. How a notification reaches a phone is decided by Home Assistant's Companion app (see its documentation). Home Assistant itself can also send GlucoCraft's data elsewhere, according to the user's own settings, for example in backups, through remote access, or to voice assistants and other services to which GlucoCraft's entities are exposed. Wall panels, if any are used, download their data from Home Assistant on the local network only, and this download is not encrypted. Any cloud service used to bring CGM data into Home Assistant (for example the CGM manufacturer's service) is governed by that service's own terms. The authors are not a "covered entity" or "business associate" under HIPAA, and they provide no service that processes the user's data.

• Readings are stored in a file in Home Assistant, in mg/dL, and retained for {retention} days. Home Assistant's own recorder history and long-term statistics of the GlucoCraft sensors are kept by Home Assistant under its own settings (see {sec:retention|Data Kept and CSV Export}). Laboratory A1C results are stored in Home Assistant; report PDFs are kept in the folder glucocraft_reports (the last 12) and CSV exports in the folder glucocraft_exports (the last 12); neither folder is accessible from the web.
• Removing GlucoCraft. What deleting GlucoCraft removes, and what it and Home Assistant keep, is described in {sec:install|Installing, Updating and Removing GlucoCraft}.

• GlucoCraft has no analytics or telemetry. Glucose data originate from the CGM's own services and reach Home Assistant through the integration in use. GlucoCraft wall panels, where used, download them from a local, read-only address that is refused from outside the home network (see the security notice below). The panels' logs show the name of the file requested, not the address.
Wall Panels

GlucoCraft wall panels are optional ESPHome devices built from GlucoCraft's example panel configurations. They are listed on Maintenance and show the same 17 pages as the display card: the seven graph pages, the nine weekly pages and the About page (About GlucoCraft: GlucoCraft's icon, the {sec:disclaimer|Disclaimer}, the version and the copyright line). A panel shows a start-up screen with GlucoCraft's icon, its name, its version and the line For development and testing only. Not for medical use. for 15 seconds at every start (a swipe ends it earlier). GlucoCraft's example panel configurations cover five panel types, the panels they were developed and tested on; another display needs a configuration of its own:
<table>
<tr><th>Panel</th><th>Screen</th><th>Display card of the same shape</th><th>Smallest text</th></tr>
Guition 480 × 480480 × 480, LCDSquare12 px (1.8 mm)
Guition 3.5-inch480 × 320, LCDRectangular (close)12 px (1.8 mm)
Waveshare LCD-7800 × 480, LCDRectangular14 px (2.7 mm)
Waveshare LCD-51024 × 600, LCDRectangular (close)14 px (1.5 mm)
Waveshare P4 7B1024 × 600, LCDRectangular (close)14 px (2.1 mm)
The panels use much smaller text than the dashboard, and the text is physically smaller on the smaller panels; a larger panel shows larger text.
Pages and Controls
<ul>

• Changing pages. The pages are changed by swiping: left anywhere on the screen for the next page, right for the previous page; the pages form one cycle. Pressing and holding the glucose block for 1 second on a graph page opens the first weekly page (when weekly values exist); pressing and holding the weekly information for 1 second returns to the 6-hour page. After 3 minutes without a touch, the 6-hour page is shown. The panels have no on-screen buttons.

• Display card. The page buttons under the display (previous and next), or a swipe on a touch screen (left for the next page), change the page; the pages form one cycle. Selecting the glucose block on a graph page opens the first weekly page, when weekly values exist; selecting the weekly information returns to the 6-hour page. After 3 minutes without use, the 6-hour page is shown, except while one of the card's buttons has the focus or the pointer is over the card; the card option Return to the first page after 3 minutes (in the card's editor; on by default) turns this off, and the page shown then stays. Every control can also be used with the keyboard (see {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}).

• Status bar (display card and wall panels). Left: Reading: 3 min ago, the whole minutes since the measurement time of the newest reading, rounded down, up to Reading: 99 min ago, and from 100 minutes the whole hours, rounded down (Reading: 1 h ago, Reading: 2 h ago); it is the age of the reading, not the time the screen was updated (Reading: --- before any reading, and while the reading's time is more than 5 minutes ahead of the clock). Middle: Warm-up: 12 min, the minutes since GlucoCraft recognized a sensor warm-up (not the time remaining), or Custom ranges while the ranges in use differ from the consensus ranges; while a GlucoCraft notice is open in Repairs, also Check Home Assistant, taking turns with them. Right: Sensor Exp: 3d 4h (or 5h 12m, 42m), the time remaining until the expiry stated by the sensor-expiry entity; Sensor expiry passed once it has passed, fading in and out until a new sensor is recognized; nothing without an expiry entity. The color of the bar is the status color (see {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}).

• No current reading. Without a current reading the place of the value shows words, never a number: Sensor warming up during a sensor warm-up; after the No current data after interval Sensor expired once the expiry time stated by the sensor-expiry entity has passed, else No current data. Under the words, smaller, the last reading (Last reading: 64 mg/dL; a reading outside the sensor's range Last reading: LO or Last reading: HI) and when it was taken with its age (Today at 17:39 (2 h 0 min ago); Yesterday at ... or the date for an older reading; the age in minutes, in hours and minutes, or in days and hours), in Home Assistant's time zone and the time and date formats set under {screen_units}; on the square display card and the square and 3.5-inch wall panels the age is on a line of its own. Without any reading only the words are shown; a wall panel keeps the last reading across a restart. No zone word is shown, the TREND column and the 5-minute delta show ---, and the status bar keeps the age of the reading (for example Reading: 2 h ago) and the status. The words throb for the first 30 minutes of each episode unless Fade the words when there is no current reading is off; the lines under them stay still. While readings still arrive after the stated expiry, the value keeps its zone color with its zone word, trend (arrow or word) and 5-minute delta, and the red status bar shows Sensor expiry passed, until a later expiry time is received. A reading beyond the sensor's range is shown as the LO / HI screen (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}), and a wall panel without Home Assistant for an hour shows Cannot reach Home Assistant or load its data (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}). GlucoCraft does not observe the sensor itself, only the stated expiry (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).

• Graphs. The graphs of 24 hours to 6 months draw, for each time slot (one pixel column: on the square card and panel about 4 minutes at 24 hours and about 13 hours at 6 months), the lowest to the highest reading (Min to max, the light-gray area with a black edge) and the mean of the readings (Mean, the white line over a black underlay); the 6-hour graph draws the readings themselves. The weekly pages are described in {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}. The graphs of 24 hours to 6 months, the statistics of 7 days and longer and the weekly pages come from GlucoCraft's full data file, which the display card and the wall panels download every hour and soon after a change of the settings the file carries, so they can be up to an hour behind the current reading (the weekly values, calculated hourly, up to about two hours). The 6-hour graph follows each reading; the 6- and 24-hour statistics are updated every 5 minutes.

• Labels and units. The short labels of the statistics, the status bar and the graph key are defined in the {sec:glossary|Glossary}. Glucose values, the 5-minute delta and the axis labels are in the display unit (mg/dL or mmol/L, see {sec:setup|Setup}), which is not repeated beside each number. GMI is shown in the A1C and GMI unit setting: on the display card with its unit (6.5%, 48 mmol/mol); the wall panels, and the statistics row under the graphs of the square display card, have no room for the unit mmol/mol and show 6.5%, 48 (mmol/mol) or 6.5%/48 (both units). The panels cite sources in short form (author and year, for example (Battelino 2019)); the full references are in {sec:references|References}.
• Square panel, weekly pages. On the 480 × 480 panel the weekly pages show a small current value at the top right; the square display card shows the current value on the graph pages only.
• Panel added. When a panel is connected for the first time, the notification GlucoCraft Panel Added names its shape and the display card in use, and where the card is changed.

• Panel offline. When a panel's Status entity has been off or unavailable for 10 minutes, the notification GlucoCraft Panel Offline states that what the panel shows may be out of date; it is removed when the panel is connected again.

Security notice. A wall panel built from the example panel configurations has two connections. Its connection with Home Assistant through the ESPHome API (the panel's entities, and firmware updates over the network) is encrypted with the panel's own API key from its secrets.yaml. Its data download, the files it reads from GlucoCraft's wall-panel address, is not encrypted: it is plain HTTP over the local network. That address is read-only, answers only on the local network and is protected by its secret id. GlucoCraft's log never names the id; Home Assistant's own log names it when a request from outside the local network reaches the address, and while debug logging is on for Home Assistant's webhook component, so a shared Home Assistant log with such a line has exposed the address. Devices on the same home network could read the downloaded data or, by posing as Home Assistant, send false data to a panel. The panels' downloaded data are therefore only as private as the home network.
docs.section.accessibility.title: Accessibility
docs.section.accessibility.body: About This Section

This section describes how GlucoCraft's dashboard cards, display cards, CGM Report and notifications, and its example wall-panel configurations, are designed for people who use a screen reader, the keyboard, a larger text size or who see colors differently. GlucoCraft is designed to follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA {cite:wcag22}, where it applies. Its known limitations, how it was checked and the conformance statement are listed at the end of this section.
What Home Assistant Provides

The page frame, the sidebar, the settings screens, the themes and the Companion apps are part of Home Assistant, and their accessibility is Home Assistant's. This section covers only the parts that GlucoCraft draws: its cards on the dashboard, the display cards, the CGM Report and its PDF, the text of its notifications and the wall panels.
Screen Readers
<ul>

• Reading order. Where the current glucose is shown (the display cards and the Last Reading of the statistics), it is read in this order: the data status, only when there is a problem (No current data. Last reading 2 hours ago., Sensor expired., Sensor warming up.; on the display cards without a current reading with the last reading, when it was taken and its age: No current data. Last reading 64 milligrams per deciliter, today at 5:39 PM, 2 hours ago.); the value with its unit written out and its zone word (Glucose 62 milligrams per deciliter, low. or Glucose 3.4 millimoles per liter, low.); the time of the reading (Measured 5 minutes ago.); the trend (Changing slowly, minus 3 milligrams per deciliter in 5 minutes.); then one sentence on what the page shows (6-hour graph: lowest 58, highest 160 milligrams per deciliter.). Without a current reading the display card reads the words shown in place of the value first, as a sentence (No current data., Sensor expired., Sensor warming up.), then the last reading with when it was taken and its age (Last reading 64 milligrams per deciliter, today at 5:39 PM, 2 hours ago.; only the value, or only the age, where the rest is not known) and the page sentence, without a value, zone word or trend; after the stated sensor expiry, while readings still arrive, Sensor expired. comes before the value. During a reading beyond the sensor's range the display card reads the value as below the sensor's lower limit or above the sensor's upper limit with its zone, then since when (Since 3:12 AM, for 2 hours 5 minutes.) and the last measured value (Last measured 52 milligrams per deciliter at 3:10 AM.). While a GlucoCraft notice is open in Repairs, Check Home Assistant. is read before the page sentence.

• Units in words. Units are read as words, because screen readers mispronounce unit symbols: milligrams per deciliter, millimoles per liter, percent, minutes, hours, days; the trend arrows as their trend words; LO and HI as below the sensor's lower limit and above the sensor's upper limit; a comparison sign before a number in words (less than, more than, at most, at least, for example less than 4 percent). In the tables of the dashboard and the CGM Report the symbols are shown and their words are read.

• Charts and tables. Every chart has a one-sentence description of the data it shows (for example the lowest, highest and mean value). Results are in tables with column and row headers, and every table has a name.

• Announcements. A banner (No current data, Sensor expired and the others) is announced once when it appears; the messages of the CGM Report page (PDF created, an error) and of the CSV export are announced; a page change on the display card is announced with the page's number, its name and its sentence.
  • New values are not announced. A new reading changes the description of the display card but is not spoken by itself; the card is read again to hear the latest value.
Keyboard and Focus

Every control that GlucoCraft draws can be reached with the Tab key and used with Enter (a button also with Space), and the focused control is outlined. The focus stays on the control that was used when a card or a page is drawn again, for example with a new reading or after a choice on the CGM Report page. Links are real links, which can also be opened in a new tab, and a link that opens a new tab says so. The choice buttons of the CGM Report page (period, form, colors) announce which one is chosen and show it with a check mark. Each section of this Documentation is a heading with a button that says whether the section is expanded; a section link or a citation moves the focus to its target. The display card's page buttons and its glucose block (which opens the weekly pages) are buttons as well, so no swipe is needed, and the card stays on its page while it is in use. Each button and link is named for where it leads (Next page: 24 hours, Open Consensus Ranges).
Color Is Never the Only Cue

Every meaning shown by a color is also shown in words or symbols: the zone word under the glucose value (Very low, Low, In range, Tight range, High, Very high; in every setting), ✓ and ✗ with their words, the status words (No current data, Sensor expired, Warm-up, Sensor expiry passed, Check Home Assistant), and the icon and the line of the Maintenance button (No issues, or the number of issues; read as Maintenance: no issues). See {sec:ranges|Ranges, Terminology and Colors}, Color Is Never the Only Cue.

Both default palettes were checked with a simulation of protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia {cite:machado2009} and the color difference CIEDE2000. In the range colors, the low and the tight-range colors become nearly identical with deuteranopia (difference 1.9); the zone word names the range in every zone. In the graph range colors as drawn (at 60% over the graph's black area), several pairs come close under each simulation, among them bands that lie next to each other (the closest: the tight-range and the very-high band with protanopia, difference 4.5); a graph is therefore not read by its colors alone: its number scale gives the glucose value of each band, and the white glucose line is read against that scale.
Contrast
The contrast ratio is calculated as defined by WCAG {cite:wcag22}: at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large text (the glucose value) and graphical elements. Measured with the default colors:
<table>
<tr><th>Pair</th><th>Contrast</th><th>Minimum</th></tr>

Glucose value, very high #1565C0 on black3.65:13:1 (large text)
Glucose value, the other display colors (#EF5350, #FFC107, #4CAF50, #42A5F5) on black6.02:1 to 12.88:13:1 (large text)
White graph text on the very-low band (#9B1C1F at 60% over the graph's #0A0A0A)12.91:14.5:1
White graph text on the low band (#E5352B)8.72:14.5:1
White graph text on the in-range bands outside the tight range (#1F8F45)8.30:14.5:1
White graph text on the tight-range band (#52B964)5.71:14.5:1
White graph text on the high band (#FCC21B)4.11:14.5:1: below (see Known Limitations)
White graph text on the very-high band (#F08A4B)5.74:14.5:1
The status bar's text is black or white, whichever has the higher contrast with the status color. The very-low and very-high display colors are used only for the large glucose value, LO and HI.
Custom Colors, Graph Range Colors and Backgrounds
<ul>

• What can be changed ({screen_displays}): the seven range colors, the seven graph range colors, the background of the display card (the Home Assistant theme or a color) and the background of the wall panels (a color); each set has its restore option. The words described above remain with any colors.

• Text on the background. On a chosen background color, the text is black or white, whichever has the higher contrast; one of the two always reaches at least 4.58:1. The secondary text colors are mixed from the text color toward the background and kept at 4.5:1 or more. The words shown in place of the value without a current reading (No current data, Sensor expired, Sensor warming up) are drawn in the text color as well. With the Home Assistant theme as the background, the theme's text color is used.
• The graphs stay on black (#0A0A0A, with white lines and labels) on every background, so that the bands and the line keep their contrast.

• Outline text ({screen_displays}; off by default). A thin 1-pixel edge around the graph labels, the glucose value, LO / HI and every other text drawn in a range color, on the display card and every wall panel: black around light text, white around dark text. It is intended for light backgrounds and light graph bands. The contrast values above are measured without the edge.

• The contrast of chosen colors is measured on the settings screen: the description at the top of the screen states in one sentence that all saved colors meet the minimum contrast on the saved background, or lists those below it. It also measures the graphs' white labels on each graph range color as drawn, at 60% over the graph's black area, against 4.5:1; with the default graph range colors it lists the yellow high band (4.1:1, the measured 4.11:1 rounded down). The sentence does not change any color; the chosen colors are always used. A light background lowers the contrast of light range colors: on white, the default amber, tight-range and high colors reach 1.63:1, 2.78:1 and 2.65:1.
Text Size and Zoom

Text on the dashboard is at least 14 px and follows the browser's zoom. The display cards draw their statistics labels at the size of the matching wall panel (12 px on the square card, as on the 480 × 480 panel) and every other text at 14 px or more; below its design width a display card draws a compact layout in which no text is below 14 px. A display card keeps one size on every page and in every state, as the wall panels do. The layouts are designed to reflow down to a width of 320 CSS pixels {cite:wcag22}: the pages card on Start then lets its lines wrap, and its rows grow with their text instead of cutting it off. The smallest text of each wall panel, in pixels and millimeters, is listed in {sec:privacy|Privacy and Wall Panels}; the physical size depends on the screen, and a larger panel shows larger text.
Notifications

GlucoCraft's notifications are plain text, which a phone's screen reader reads as written. The title names the notification (GlucoCraft Daily Summary). The body writes the glucose unit in words (for example 112 milligrams per deciliter), the trend as its trend words (for example changing slowly), without arrow symbols, a LO or HI reading in words, and the measurement time. No information is carried by color or emoji alone (see {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}).
The CGM Report and Its PDF

The CGM Report page of the dashboard is the alternative to the PDF: its section titles are headings, its tables have column and row headers, the units of its tables are read in words, and each chart has a one-sentence description of its data. The PDF has the same content and is tagged for screen readers: its section titles are headings, its tables have column and row headers, each chart has the same one-sentence description as on the page, its content is read in the order of the page, and it states its document language; a target with a comparison sign is read in words, and its headings are its bookmarks. The PDF passes the checks of PDF/UA-1 (ISO 14289-1), the specification for accessible PDF files, made by the open-source validator veraPDF, and names PDF/UA-1 in its metadata. The CGM Report page remains an alternative to the PDF.
Voice
<ul>

• Spoken summary. The sensor sensor.glucocraft_spoken_summary (Spoken summary) has as its state one ready-to-speak sentence, a shorter form of the screen-reader text built with the same words and in the same order: the data status when there is a problem, the value with its unit and the range, the time of the reading and the trend, without the 5-minute delta and the page sentence (during a sensor warm-up only Sensor warming up.), for example Glucose 112 milligrams per deciliter, tight range, measured at 7:46 AM, changing slowly., or No current data. Last reading at 7:46 AM. The time is written in the time format setting; a reading of an earlier day is named with its day (Last reading yesterday at 9:45 PM., or with its date in the date format setting, Last reading on October 22 at 9:45 PM.). The sentence changes only with a new reading, a change of status, no current data, zone, trend or LO / HI, a change of the display unit, the decimal separator or the time or date format, and at midnight, so it names the time of the reading and not its age, which would no longer be correct a minute later. It is disabled by default, because every new sentence adds to Home Assistant's recorded history. To enable it: Settings > Devices & services > Entities, search for Spoken summary, select it, open its settings and turn on Enabled.

• Voice assistants. GlucoCraft ships no voice intents. Its entities are ordinary Home Assistant entities: an entity that is exposed to Assist (Settings > Voice assistants > Expose) can be read by Home Assistant's voice assistants {cite:haExpose}. Home Assistant's own question about the state of an entity answers with the entity's name and its state {cite:haIntents}, for example Glucocraft spoken summary is Glucose 112 milligrams per deciliter, …

• Example. These lines are not part of GlucoCraft; a user who wants another wording adds them to Home Assistant's configuration.yaml. They add the sentence read the GlucoCraft Spoken summary to Home Assistant's own question about the state of an entity {cite:haSentences}:
    # Example: added by the user; GlucoCraft ships no voice intents.
conversation:
  intents:
    HassGetState:
      - "read [the] {name}"
Motion and Timing
<ul>

• Nothing on the dashboard and the display cards flashes, and only two things move: words that fade, and the section links of this Documentation, which scroll. While there is no current reading, the words Sensor warming up, Sensor expired or No current data in place of the value on the display cards and the wall panels fade to about 30% brightness and back, once every 3 seconds (about 0.33 Hz, far below the limit of three flashes per second of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines), for the first 30 minutes of each episode; then they hold still. After the stated sensor expiry, the status bar's Sensor expiry passed fades in the same way for as long as the expiry has passed: it is small text, and putting on a new sensor can take a while. They never disappear, and screen readers read the same text throughout. The setting Fade the words when there is no current reading turns both off, and the display cards stop them while the system's reduced-motion setting is on (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}). The Documentation's section links scroll smoothly to their section, and at once, without motion, while the system's reduced-motion setting is on.

• Timing. The display card returns to its first page after 3 minutes without use, but not while one of its buttons has the focus or the pointer is over it; a screen reader that reads a page without moving the focus does not hold it. The card setting Return to the first page turns this off. The wall panels show their start-up screen for 15 seconds at every start (a swipe ends it earlier); the {sec:disclaimer|Disclaimer} is always available on the page About GlucoCraft of the panels and the display cards (page 17 of 17 on the display card).
Wall Panels

The example wall-panel configurations are visual only: a panel built from them cannot be read by a screen reader, and a person who is blind cannot use it. The same pages are available on the display card, which has screen-reader text, and the current value, its range and the trend can also be heard through the Spoken summary sensor (disabled by default) and a voice assistant (see Voice).
Plain Language

GlucoCraft's texts use full words and avoid abbreviations where possible. The abbreviations of the published report format (TIR, TITR, CV, GMI, GRI, SD) are used in tables and defined in {sec:metrics|Metrics and Sources}; the short labels of the display card and the wall panels are defined in the {sec:glossary|Glossary}.
Known Limitations
<table>
<tr><th>Limitation</th><th>Reason</th><th>Alternative</th></tr>

A panel built from the example wall-panel configurations cannot be read by a screen reader.The examples are visual displays without speech output.The display card shows the same pages with screen-reader text; the current value, its range and the trend can also be heard through the Spoken summary sensor (disabled by default) and a voice assistant (see Voice).

12 px text: the statistics labels of the square 480 × 480 panel and the 3.5-inch 480 × 320 panel; on the 3.5-inch panel also TREND, 5 MIN DELTA, the source name, the weekly description line and the GMI value in both A1C units; and the statistics labels of the square display card.The screens of the two small example panels are small; the square display card matches the 480 × 480 panel.A larger panel, or the display card at the browser's zoom.

White graph text on the default high band reaches 4.11:1. The light-gray key --- Min to max above the period graphs is below 4.5:1 on four default bands: 2.19:1 on the high band, 3.05:1 on the very-high band, 3.04:1 on the tight-range band and 4.42:1 on the in-range bands.The graph text is white on every band, as on the panels.The same values are in the statistics beside each graph and in the text description.

A new reading is not announced by a screen reader.The dashboard announces its banners, not each reading.Reading the display card again; the CGM system's own app, reader or receiver.

How This Was Checked
<ul>

• Automatic checks, run with GlucoCraft's tests: the contrast of every text and background pair that the cards draw, with both default backgrounds (black and white) and the default palettes; the color-vision simulation of both default palettes {cite:machado2009}, which reports every pair below a CIEDE2000 difference of 10 and checks that words cover it; and checks that every card and chart has a text description, every button and link has a name, every link has an address, nothing that can be focused is hidden from screen readers, the focus stays on its control when a card is drawn again, the state of the choice buttons and the status messages are announced, and units, trend arrows and comparison signs are read in words.
• Review: every page, card and the PDF were reviewed against WCAG 2.2 level AA {cite:wcag22} and the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices {cite:apg}.
• Testers: people who use a screen reader, the keyboard or browser zoom are invited to report anything that is read wrongly, cannot be reached or is hard to see (see Feedback).

• Conformance. GlucoCraft is designed to follow WCAG 2.2 level AA where it applies. No conformance claim is made. Known limitations are listed above. GlucoCraft does not claim to be accessible or to meet WCAG or any other standard.
Feedback

Accessibility problems are welcome as bug reports at https://github.com/Verstreubulator/glucocraft, with the area Accessibility. It helps to name the screen reader or browser and its version, the page, and what was heard or seen. No response time is promised.
docs.section.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
docs.section.troubleshooting.body: Each entry states the symptom, its usual cause and what to check. Every repair notice of GlucoCraft is listed, with when it appears, in {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}. The diagnostics file (Settings > Devices & services > GlucoCraft > the menu (three dots) > Download diagnostics) contains GlucoCraft's settings, its version, the number of stored readings and the time span they cover, the reading interval, the state of the sources, the status and the time of the last reading, the open repair notices, the state of the wall-panel address, the models and versions of the wall panels, the language, and Home Assistant's country with the regional formats it gives. It contains no glucose value, no reading and no laboratory result, and no custom range limits or goals: in their place it states only whether custom ranges are in use and whether custom goals are set; the entity ids of the sources (also the sensor-expiry entity), the phones' notify actions, the printer address, the wall-panel id and every stored setting that GlucoCraft does not know are replaced by **REDACTED**, and an open repair notice about a source names the source's role (primary_source or secondary_source) in place of its entity id. Home Assistant's log (Settings > System > Logs) shows one warning when the source in use becomes unavailable or sends no reading for longer than the no-current-data limit; it is not repeated while that lasts. GlucoCraft's log names a phone's notify action only by its position among the chosen ones; Home Assistant's log names the phone itself when its Mobile App integration cannot deliver a message to it.
<ul>

• No current data. Symptom: the status shows No current data, the display card and the wall panels show No current data in place of the glucose value, and the trend values are shown as unknown; the status bar shows the age of the last reading. Cause: no new measurement has arrived for {stale} minutes: the source entity has not updated, is unavailable, or receives its readings late from its app, cloud service or integration. While stored readings are more than 5 minutes later than the system clock, no reading is stored, and a repair notice explains why. Check: the source entity's state and its last update in Developer tools > States; the integration that provides it; the sources on the Maintenance page; No current data after on the screen {screen_sources}; Settings > System > Repairs.

• The source updates slowly. Symptom: the repair notice Glucose source is too slow for live display. Cause: the median of the source's last 10 reading intervals is 15 minutes or longer; such a source is not supported for live display (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}). The interval is the source's own (the update interval of the integration that provides it, or of the service it reads), not a GlucoCraft setting. Check: the reading interval on the Maintenance page and the options of the integration that provides the source (see {sec:cgms|Supported Sources}).

• The value stays the same for over an hour. Symptom: the repair notice Glucose source may have stopped: the same value for over an hour. Cause: a source without its own measurement time has delivered exactly the same value 12 times or more in a row, over at least 60 minutes; GlucoCraft cannot tell a source that keeps sending its last value from a steady glucose level. Check: the steps in the notice: the CGM sensor and its app; an attribute with the time of each measurement in Developer tools > States, entered as Measurement-time attribute on the screen {screen_sources} (see {sec:cgms|Supported Sources}). The notice closes by itself when the value changes.
  • LO or HI shown at the sensor's limit. Symptom: the words Very low or Very high with Below sensor range (LO) or Above sensor range (HI) in place of the value, LO or HI in the Statistics table, small marks along the bottom or the top edge of the graphs, and a note under the statistics about readings at the sensor's limit. Cause: the source passed a reading outside the CGM sensor's measurement range (a text such as LO / HI, a code number, or a number at or beyond the limit); GlucoCraft shows it as LO / HI and leaves it out of the calculated values. A measured value shown as LO or HI, or readings that stop at exactly {value_400} or {value_450} {unit}, or at {value_50} {unit} (a repair notice is then raised), can mean that the sensor limits in the settings do not match the CGM system; the repair notices about limits (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}) say which. Check: Sensor lower limit and Sensor upper limit of each source on the screen {screen_sources}, and {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}, which lists the measurement ranges.

• A repair notice about a very-low or very-high limit. Symptom: the repair notice The very-low limit is below the glucose sensor's lower limit or The very-high limit is above the glucose sensor's upper limit. Cause: a source or its sensor limit changed after the ranges were saved; GlucoCraft uses the sensor's limit instead. Check: the sensor limits on the screen {screen_sources} and the ranges on the screen Glucose ranges; the notice closes by itself when the setting fits again (see {sec:lohi|Readings Outside the Sensor's Range (LO / HI)}).

• A GlucoCraft entity is set as a glucose source. Symptom: the repair notice of that name. Cause: an entity of GlucoCraft itself was chosen as a source; its values are GlucoCraft's own and are not used. Check: the sources on the screen {screen_sources}: the CGM integration's sensor is the source. The notice closes when another source is chosen.

• The glucose source is not found or has another unit. Symptom: the repair notice Glucose source not found, Glucose source with a unit other than mg/dL or mmol/L or Glucose source without a unit. Cause: the source entity no longer exists (its integration was removed or set up again, or it received a new entity id while GlucoCraft was not running; while GlucoCraft runs, it follows a new entity id), it states a unit other than mg/dL or mmol/L, or it states no unit while its values indicate mmol/L (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Unit). Check: the sources on the screen {screen_sources} and the entity's unit of measurement in Developer tools > States.

• GlucoCraft's entity ids were changed. Symptom: the repair notice GlucoCraft put its entity ids back or Entity ids of GlucoCraft were changed; with the second, the display card and the wall panels can show No current data while readings still arrive. Cause: an entity id of GlucoCraft was changed, by hand or together with a new name for the device. GlucoCraft's cards, its dashboard and the wall panels find their entities by the original ids, which is necessary for GlucoCraft to continue to function properly. Check: the first notice needs nothing: GlucoCraft has already given the original ids back. It lists them and stays until it is dismissed (Ignore). The second notice is for a change GlucoCraft could not undo: one made while it was not running, or one whose original id another entity has. Open the notice and submit it to give the original ids back; the recorded history stays with the entities. Automations, dashboards and other items that were pointed at the changed ids then have to be pointed back. If another entity has an original id, rename or delete that entity and open the notice again.

• LO, HI or no current data from a source with the wrong unit. Symptom: the repair notice Glucose source states mg/dL with values that look like mmol/L or Glucose source states mmol/L with values that look like another unit; the display shows LO, HI or No current data although the sensor is working. Cause: the source's values are in another unit than the one it states. GlucoCraft cannot tell this from one value, so it treats them in the stated unit and says so after 10 readings in a row. LO or HI shown this way is not a measurement. Check: the entity's unit of measurement in Developer tools > States, and the unit in its template sensor if it has one; or choose another source on the screen {screen_sources}. The notice closes by itself with the next plausible value. Readings already stored are not changed.

• A repair notice about the readings file. Symptom: a repair notice says that GlucoCraft's readings file was damaged, could not be read or is from a newer version of GlucoCraft. Cause: the file in the glucocraft folder of the Home Assistant configuration was damaged or could not be opened (a storage or permission error), or a newer version of GlucoCraft wrote it. A damaged file is kept aside under the name in the notice; GlucoCraft recovers what it can, or starts with an empty history that it fills from Home Assistant's recorder where it still holds the readings. A file that could not be read is not written to until GlucoCraft starts again (a restart of Home Assistant, or a reload of GlucoCraft, which saving its settings also does); readings received in the meantime are kept in memory only. They are lost when GlucoCraft starts again, except those Home Assistant's recorder still holds for the glucose source, which GlucoCraft imports again then. A file written by a newer version of GlucoCraft (after an older version was installed over it) is neither read nor written by the older version; installing the newer version again uses it. Readings more than a year later than the system clock are not damage when they end the file in time order (at least 3 of them, or all the readings of the file): the clock is then taken to be behind, the readings are kept, and the notice Stored glucose readings are later than the system clock applies. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. Check: the text of the notice; the storage of the Home Assistant host; a backup made before the damage, restored while Home Assistant is stopped.

• The readings file could not be written. Symptom: the repair notice GlucoCraft's readings file could not be written, or a notice about a damaged readings file that says no copy of the file could be kept. Cause: the storage of the Home Assistant host is full or read-only, or the glucocraft folder cannot be written; readings received in the meantime are kept in memory only and are lost at a restart. Check: the free space of the Home Assistant host and the permissions of the glucocraft folder of the Home Assistant configuration; the notice closes by itself when the file is written again (the notices about a damaged file at the next start at which a copy can be kept).

• The cards could not be added. Symptom: the repair notice GlucoCraft's cards could not be added to the dashboards; GlucoCraft's dashboard or its cards may not load. Cause: Home Assistant did not accept GlucoCraft's card files as dashboard resources. Check: add them by hand: with Advanced mode on in the user profile, Settings > Dashboards > the menu (three dots) > Resources > Add resource, each of /glucocraft/glucocraft-display-card.js, /glucocraft/glucocraft-strategy.js, /glucocraft/glucocraft-ui.js, /glucocraft/glucocraft-docs.js and /glucocraft/glucocraft-report.js with the resource type JavaScript module; the notice closes by itself at the next start of GlucoCraft at which the resources are added.

• A wall panel is offline. Symptom: the notice GlucoCraft Panel Offline, when the panel's Status entity has been off or unavailable for 10 minutes; the panel's status on the Maintenance page, where it is listed under Maintenance issues. Cause: the panel has no power or no network connection, or it cannot reach Home Assistant. A panel that is connected but receives no data uses an address that is no longer valid (a new wall-panel address was created), or Home Assistant does not see its request as coming from the local network. Check: the panel's power and network connection; the panel in Settings > Devices & services > ESPHome; that the id of the wall-panel address in the panel's configuration (in the example panel configurations: glucocraft_panel_webhook_id in secrets.yaml) is the one shown on the screen {screen_displays}.
  • A wall panel shows Cannot reach Home Assistant or load its data. Symptom: below the clock and the date, the panel is black with Cannot reach Home Assistant or load its data, since when, the last reading and Check Home Assistant and the wall-panel address. Cause: for an hour, the panel has had no connection to Home Assistant (Home Assistant not running, Wi-Fi or the network lost, the panel's entry disabled), or it could not download GlucoCraft's data (an address that is no longer valid). Check: that Home Assistant is running; the panel's power and network connection and the panel in Settings > Devices & services > ESPHome; that the id of the wall-panel address in the panel's configuration is the one shown on the screen {screen_displays}. The screen clears by itself when both work again (see {sec:gaps|Gaps, Reading Interval and No Current Data}).
  • Check Home Assistant in the status bar. Symptom: the display card and the wall panels show Check Home Assistant in the middle of the status bar. Cause: a GlucoCraft notice is open in Home Assistant's Repairs. Check: Settings > System > Repairs: the notice states what happened and what to do. Check Home Assistant goes away when the notice closes, or when Ignore is chosen on it.
  • Reading: --- in the status bar. Symptom: the status bar shows Reading: --- while readings arrive, and no time is shown under the words. Cause: the newest reading's time is more than 5 minutes ahead of Home Assistant's clock, so its age is not known. Check: the explanation on the Maintenance page; Home Assistant's clock and time zone (Settings > System > General); on the display card, also the clock of the device it is shown on.
  • A repair notice about the sensor expiry entity. Symptom: CGM sensor expiry entity not found, CGM sensor expiry entity holds no expiry or CGM sensor expiry entity shows an expiry long past. Cause: the entity set as CGM sensor expiry entity does not exist, holds no expiry, or holds another time or has stopped updating. Check: the entity on the screen {screen_sources}: the CGM integration's entity that holds the sensor's expiry, or clear the setting.

• Wall panels show no current data after a new wall-panel address was created. Symptom: every wall panel shows that no current data arrives, from the moment Create a new wall-panel address was submitted. Cause: the earlier address stopped working, and each panel's firmware still contains the earlier id. Check: the steps of Creating or changing the wall-panel address in {sec:setup|Setup}: copy the new id from the screen {screen_displays}, replace the id in each panel's configuration (in the example panel configurations: glucocraft_panel_webhook_id in secrets.yaml), build and install every panel again, and check that each panel shows current data again.

• History not available. Symptom: the wall panel and the display card show Loading... in the graphs and on the weekly pages until a download works (the display card tries again every minute); at its start a wall panel may show History not available and Showing live data for a second, often hidden by the start-up screen. Cause: the history file could not be downloaded (no readings stored yet, Home Assistant restarting, or, for a panel, an address that is no longer valid). Check: reload the page; for a panel, the steps under A wall panel is offline.

• A wall panel shows an old version after an update. Symptom: the panel's About page, its device information or the Maintenance page shows a version older than that of the example panel configurations. Cause: updating GlucoCraft does not change a panel's firmware. The panel runs the firmware that ESPHome built from the example panel configuration. Check: building the firmware again with ESPHome from the updated example configuration and installing it on the panel brings the panel to that version.

• The CGM Report PDF does not print. Symptom: the notification GlucoCraft CGM Report states that the report was not printed, and the action glucocraft.print_report reports an error; for a period or an appendix that is not available, only the action reports the error, and no notification is created. Cause: no printer address is set, the period is not one of 14, 30, 90 or 180 days (This report period is not available: …), the appendix Custom Ranges and Goals was chosen while Custom ranges and goals is off, the PDF could not be created (nothing is then sent or kept), the printer cannot be reached, or it does not accept IPP (on port 631 unless the address names another port). When a printer address is set and the PDF could be created, it is kept in glucocraft_reports, under the file name in the notification. Check: the reason in the notification; Report printer on the screen {screen_report} (a host, or an ipp://, ipps://, http:// or https:// address, without a user name or password); that the printer is switched on and can be reached from Home Assistant at that address. ipps:// and https:// work only with a printer certificate that Home Assistant trusts; most printers' own certificates are not trusted, and the print then fails (the notification then states that the printer's certificate is not trusted). The PDF can also be downloaded on the CGM Report page.

• More detail in Home Assistant's log. Symptom: a problem that the entries above do not explain. Cause: GlucoCraft writes its warnings and errors to Home Assistant's log; the detail of each step only at the debug level. Check: Settings > Devices & services > GlucoCraft > the menu (three dots) > Enable debug logging; after the problem has occurred again, Disable debug logging downloads the log. A debug log names entities and folders of the installation; read it and remove names before sharing it.

• The dashboard does not change after an update. Symptom: after an update of GlucoCraft and the restart of Home Assistant, an open dashboard page still shows the earlier version. Cause: the page was loaded before the update and still runs the earlier card files. Check: reload the page once. Cards added by hand to other dashboards through the unversioned address /glucocraft/... may need the browser's hard refresh; the browser console shows the version of each card file.

• A label is blank or a new setting is missing after an update. Symptom: after an update of GlucoCraft, a label on a dashboard page or a settings screen is empty, or a setting described in this Documentation is not shown. Cause: the browser still holds texts from before the update: Home Assistant's own texts of the settings screens, or the texts of cards added by hand through the unversioned address /glucocraft/.... Check: reload the page; if the label stays blank, use the browser's hard refresh, which reloads the page without its cache (for example Ctrl+F5 on Windows and Linux, Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac).
docs.section.limits.title: Known Limitations
docs.section.limits.body: • GlucoCraft's values are calculated from the readings it receives, which can be late, missing or wrong. CGM readings can differ from blood glucose meter readings; the CGM manufacturer's documentation states the accuracy of the CGM system.

• Values for short periods describe only that period. A period's values are shown only with at least 70% sensor active (see {sec:how|How GlucoCraft Is Designed}, Enough data); the consensus recommends at least 14 days with at least 70% sensor active {cite:battelino2019}.
• GMI is an estimate and not a laboratory A1C {cite:bergenstal2018}.

• A reading outside the sensor's measurement range (LO / HI) has no measured value; GlucoCraft leaves it out of the calculated values and counts it as very low or very high in the time in ranges, so values such as the mean can differ from those that the true values would give and from a manufacturer's report. This method is a GlucoCraft rule. The limits depend on the settings of each source, and wrong limits produce wrong LO / HI readings. {limit_note}
• Notifications may be delayed or not delivered (see {sec:notifications|Notifications (Not Alarms)}).
• Readings older than {retention} days are not kept; the 6-month report therefore has no previous period, and older laboratory results have no CGM comparison.
• The trend categories follow one manufacturer's scale {cite:abbott} for all CGM systems; GlucoCraft's trend may therefore differ from the CGM's own trend arrow.

• A wall panel that has lost power, Wi-Fi or its connection to Home Assistant can continue to show out-of-date values; the notice GlucoCraft Panel Offline appears only when the panel's Status entity has been off or unavailable for 10 minutes.

• The example wall-panel configurations are visual only: a panel built from them cannot be read by a screen reader. The smallest text of each example panel is listed in {sec:privacy|Privacy and Wall Panels} (see also {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}).

• Accessibility. White graph text on the default high band reaches 4.11:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for text. This and the other accessibility limitations are listed with their reasons and alternatives in {sec:accessibility|Accessibility}, Known Limitations.
• Every text is prepared for translation, but only English is provided; with another language set in Home Assistant, GlucoCraft shows its English texts.

How GlucoCraft is made

GlucoCraft is written with the help of an AI coding assistant, Claude (Anthropic). The maintainer directs the work and decides every design question and every public text; the code is checked by the test suite and on test installations of Home Assistant before each release.

• Material Design Icons (Pictogrammers, Apache License 2.0): the arrow drawn by the display card is the icon arrow-right. License: Apache License, Version 2.0 (its text is in GlucoCraft's file LICENSE-Apache-2.0.txt); source: github.com/Templarian/MaterialDesign.

• ReportLab (BSD license): the library that creates the CGM Report's PDF. It is installed by Home Assistant with GlucoCraft's requirements and is not part of GlucoCraft's files.
  • Liberation Sans 2.1.5 (SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1): the font of the CGM Report's PDF, bundled unmodified in GlucoCraft's fonts folder with its license and embedded in the PDF. Digitized data copyright (c) 2010 Google Corporation with Reserved Font Arimo, Tinos and Cousine; copyright (c) 2012 Red Hat, Inc. with Reserved Font Name Liberation. License: SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1; source: github.com/liberationfonts/liberation-fonts.

    • The example wall-panel configurations use further components, none of them part of GlucoCraft's files: ESPHome, Roboto, LVGL and, on one board, ESP-Hosted (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in GlucoCraft's folder custom_components/glucocraft/).
